$2 oysters inside one of the most expensive resorts on the Strip. The Proper Eats happy hour at Aria is one of those deals that feels like it shouldn't exist — but it does, weekdays from 4–6pm at Proper Bar. Order This:
  • Fresh-shucked oysters ($2 each) — Atlantic Blue Point and rotating coast-to-coast varieties, served on ice with housemade cocktail sauce and mignonette, shucked to order
  • Gin-Z cocktail ($16) — gin, Aperol, and Prosecco; light, cold, and works well with a plate of oysters in front of you
Proper Bar sits at the center of Aria's food hall, an oval bar with floor-to-ceiling windows overlooking the pool and the desert beyond. It's a genuinely good-looking room. The food hall around it — Wexler's Deli, Seoul Bird, and others — means you can grab something serious to eat and then pull up a bar stool for the happy hour. The oyster price is the hook, but the setting is what makes it stick. Inside a casino that doesn't apologize for being expensive, two-dollar oysters on ice with a craft cocktail is a legitimate deal worth knowing about. 🦪 Mon–Fri, 4–6pm. Walk-in seating at the bar. No reservation needed for happy hour.

post_content: Board shorts optional, but the vibe at this Boca Park spot says beach bar even though the closest ocean is four hours away. Order This: Street tacos run $2 each during happy hour, so grab three or four and mix carne asada with something spicier — it's the cheapest way to sample the wild-caught fish taco lineup Wahoo's built its name on. Pair it with a $5 Wahoo's Margarita. Wahoo's happy hour in Summerlin runs twice daily, 3-6 PM and again 11 PM-2 AM, which covers the after-work crowd and the ones stumbling out of Boca Park bars looking for tacos at midnight. The Lee brothers built this menu on a mashup of Baja, Brazilian, and Asian flavors back in Costa Mesa in 1988, and the Vegas location keeps that surf-shop, no-pretense energy intact — a rarity in a neighborhood full of polished patio restaurants. It's the kind of happy hour locals keep in their back pocket for exactly the right mood. Happy hour runs daily, 3-6 PM and 11 PM-2 AM. Family-style portions at Carmine's mean one appetizer usually feeds four people — happy hour doesn't change that math, it just drops the price on top of it. Carmine's Italian Restaurant's happy hour at Caesars Palace runs Monday-Thursday, 2-4pm, at the bar only, with $10 cocktails, $8 wine, and $10 meatball sliders. Order This: The meatball sliders — a Carmine's staple sized for the table, not a solo snack, and the closest thing on the happy hour menu to the restaurant's famous portion sizes at a tenth of the commitment. The eggplant rollatini and fried zucchini round out the food list if you're staying past one round. Carmine's built its Vegas reputation on Southern Italian family-style dining — the kind of place where two people order for four and still leave with leftovers. That makes happy hour here a genuinely different animal: a two-hour window to sample the Forum Shops institution without ordering a platter meant for a birthday party. It's a smart, low-commitment entry point before you come back for the full family-style spread. Bar seating only, no reservations needed for happy hour specifically — walk up, grab a stool, and go in knowing the regular menu's portion sizes are the whole reason people love this place.

Parking:

Valet and Self Parking are available at Caesars Hotel & Casino, with only a brief walk through the world famous Forum Shops. Free 3 hour parking for Las Vegas residents.

post_content: North Las Vegas doesn't have many fine dining options, and Carve Prime Rib at the Cannery Casino is the one locals point to when someone asks. The Carve Prime Rib happy hour runs Wednesday through Sunday, 4 to 6 PM, with discounted beer, wine, cocktails and appetizers in the bar and lounge. Order This: the 40-day-aged prime rib — reviewers call it the best in town, and the bar menu gives you a reason to order it before dinner prices kick in. The Blackberry Bite cocktail — Knob Creek bourbon, blackberry mint infusion, angostura bitters, and simple syrup — is the signature drink and worth ordering once. Happy hour specials include discounted beer, wine, cocktails and appetizers; confirm current pricing at the bar. Carve is the kind of steakhouse that exists because a neighborhood needs one — not because it's chasing press or awards. The lounge and bar area have multiple TVs and a separate bar menu, so you can eat and drink well without committing to a full dinner reservation. Reviewers consistently single out the service as the thing that keeps them coming back, which says something about a casino restaurant that doesn't have the foot traffic of the Strip to coast on. If you're north of the 215 and want a proper steakhouse bar, this is where you go. Happy hour runs Wednesday through Sunday, 4 to 6 PM, in the bar and lounge. Reservations are recommended for the dining room; bar seating is walk-in.

Flanker Happy Hour

Flanker Kitchen + Sports Bar Happy Hour | Monday - Friday | 4pm - 6pm | Mandalay Bay Las Vegas

Alright, let's talk about Flanker Kitchen + Sports Bar at Mandalay Bay. Vegas. A shimmering monument to excess, a desert mirage built on the backs of broken dreams and the fleeting promise of a jackpot. And within this glittering behemoth, we find Flanker. Happy Hour. Because even the high rollers and the desperate gamblers need a break from the relentless assault on their senses. Flanker Kitchen + Sports Bar offers a unique happy hour experience that sets it apart from typical sports bars, including the pop up Tiki Bar Happy hour and the karaoke room. There is a focus on quality cuisine, top-shelf drinks, and an inviting ambiance, it has become a local favorite and is regarded as one of the best sports bars on the Strip, attracting locals and visitors.

When we asked our experts where to go to watch a game, Flanker was the hands-down favorite. Brought to you by the team behind Carversteak in Resorts World and Casa Playa in Wynn, it may be the most upscale of the many sports-themed restaurants to open over the past few years. The interior is dark. The décor is modern. The bar team is worthy of an upscale nightclub. And there’s a private dining room that converts to a private karaoke lounge.

Read more about Flanker Kitchen + Sports Bar at NEONFEAST...

Flanker Happy Hour Menu

Flanker Kitchen + Sports Bar Happy Hour Menu. That's where the story gets interesting. Or, at least, mildly diverting. You've got your usual suspects: discounted appetizers, reduced drink prices. The kind of stuff that's designed to lure you in and keep you there, wallet slightly lighter, but hopefully, spirits slightly higher. Don't expect culinary revelations. This isn't a Michelin-starred experience. This is about sustenance. Fuel. The kind of food that soaks up the booze and allows you to stumble back out into the casino, ready to lose another paycheck. See the Flanker Happy Hour Menu Here. Think sliders. Wings. Maybe some nachos piled high with enough cheese and jalapeños to give you heartburn for a week. It's not exactly haute cuisine, but it's honest. It's unpretentious. It's the kind of food that tastes exactly how you expect it to taste. And sometimes, that's exactly what you need. No surprises. No culinary acrobatics. Just good, solid, greasy, satisfying bar food.

Flanker Kitchen + Sports Bar Happy Hour Menu: Apps & Eats

Pigs In A Blanket (2pc) | 9 Spicy Honey Mustard Pretzel Bites | 9 Beer Cheese, Grain Mustard Fried Pickles | 9 Spicy Ranch Mac n Cheese Bites | 9 Parmesan, Marinara Sauce Korean Lettuce Wraps | 10 Braised Short Rib, Sesame Slaw, Gochujang Aioli Crudité | 12 Hummus, Baba Ghanoush, Fresh Veggies Street Tacos (2pc) | 9 Carne Asada, Crispy Garlic Shrimp, Shredded Chicken Half Order Crispy Wings | 12 Salt n Lemon Pepper / Buffalo / Spicy Korean The drinks. Well, what can I say? It's Vegas. Booze is the lifeblood of this town. Expect the usual suspects: beers on tap, well drinks, maybe a discounted cocktail or two. Don't go expecting some expertly crafted mixology masterpiece. This isn't that kind of place. This is about volume. Getting the drinks out fast and keeping the party going. It's a transactional relationship. You pay, they pour. Simple as that. Flanker Kitchen + Sports Bar Happy Hour Menu - Drinks Menu Margarita | 8 El Tequileno Blanco, Triple Sec, Fresh Lime Juice, Agave Smokin’ Joe Old Fashioned | 8 Jack Daniel’s Straight Rye Whiskey, Diplomático Reserva Rum, Falernum, Bitters Select Draft Beer | 8

But here's the thing. Despite the lack of pretension, despite the predictable menu, there's a certain charm to Flanker's Happy Hour. It's a refuge. A place where you can escape the relentless pressure of the casino floor, even if just for an hour or two. A place where you can grab a cheap beer, scarf down some wings, and watch the game with a bunch of strangers who are all looking for the same thing: a moment of distraction.

It's not going to change your life. It's not going to inspire you. But it's not trying to. It's just trying to offer a brief respite from the chaos. And in a city like Vegas, that's worth something. It's a reminder that even in the midst of all the glitz and glamour, there's still room for the simple pleasures. A cold beer. A hot plate of wings. The company of strangers. It's not much. But sometimes, it's enough. It's just enough. And in a place like Vegas, sometimes, just enough is a goddamn miracle.

Rí Rá Irish Pub Happy Hour

Rí Rá Irish Pub Happy Hour 3 - 6 PM & 11pm - Midnight Everyday.

Step into Ireland (without leaving Vegas) The second you walk through the door at Rí Rá, you’re transported to an authentic Irish pub. And it’s not just for show—the place is built with salvaged materials from actual pubs in Ireland. The dark wood paneling, antique mirrors, and vintage memorabilia give the place a cozy, lived-in feel that makes it easy to settle in and stay awhile. Whether you're a Vegas local or visiting from out of town, this pub instantly feels like home. Happy Hour Details You’ll Love 📅 When: Everyday 🕒 Time: 3 PM – 6 PM & 11pm - midnight 📍 Where: Bar area and select seating What really sets Rí Rá apart is the vibe. The staff is friendly and always ready with a recommendation or a good laugh. There’s often live music too—so you might find yourself tapping your foot to an acoustic Irish set or singing along with a local band. It’s fun, relaxed, and just a little rowdy (in the best way). Besides the obvious perks—great food, solid drinks, and a killer location—Rí Rá offers something extra: heart. It’s the kind of place where you can belly up to the bar and feel like a regular, even on your first visit. And the location? Right inside The Shoppes at Mandalay Place. It’s easy to get to, and makes a perfect stop whether you're heading to a concert, show, or just exploring the Strip. If you’re looking for a place that feels like a little slice of Ireland—with great food, drinks, and that warm pub atmosphere—Rí Rá is the spot. Their Happy Hour is the real deal, and the perfect excuse to slow down, sip something tasty, and enjoy the moment. Sláinte!

post_content: Scotch 80 Prime at the Palms runs its Social Hour Monday through Thursday with 30% off some of the kitchen's best dishes, which puts an 8 ounce filet for $50.40 and oysters at $17.50 for six. A Michelin-pedigreed steakhouse running daily happy hour. At Paris Las Vegas. That's the deal at Gordon Ramsay Steak, and if you've been sleeping on it, consider this your wake-up call. The happy hour at Gordon Ramsay Steak runs daily 4–6PM and features discounted cocktails and chef-level bar bites that don't exist anywhere else at this price point on the Strip. Order This:

  • Passion Mule — $11–$14: Angel's Envy bourbon, passion fruit, ginger beer, actual backbone

This happy hour exists because the room opens at 4PM and Ramsay's team knows the bar program is worth showing off before the dinner rush takes over. The two-story dining room under the Union Jack ceiling is dramatic even half-empty. You're not here to save money — you're here because $14 cocktails at this kitchen are a fraction of what dinner costs, and the food still comes out the same way it does for a $200 tab. Go early in the week if you want elbow room at the bar. 🥩 * Note

post_title: California Pizza Kitchen Happy Hour Town Square
post_content:
Restaurant-wide happy hour — not just bar seating, not just a corner booth — at California Pizza Kitchen in Town Square. Monday through Friday, the whole dining room runs $5–$9 pricing, and the 7" pizza and draft combo for $9 is one of the more underrated weekday deals in the southwest valley.

The happy hour at California Pizza Kitchen Town Square runs Monday through Friday, 3–6PM, dine-in only, with tiered pricing across drinks and small plates.

Order This:

  • $9 Pizza + Draft Beer Combo: 7" pizza (BBQ Chicken, Pepperoni, or Cheese) paired with a draft — the best per-dollar deal on the menu
  • Dynamite Shrimp — $8: crispy, saucy, disappears fast
  • Szechwan Chicken Dumplings — $8: the sleeper pick; better than you'd expect at this price
  • Spinach Artichoke Dip — $8
  • $8 Signature Cocktails, Sangrias, Margaritas, and Mules | $7 wine (6oz) | $5 draft and bottled beer

CPK runs this restaurant-wide, which means you're not stuck at a noisy bar fighting for a stool — you can grab a full table and order like it's dinner, because it basically is. The Town Square location has outdoor patio access and is a natural stop before or after a movie. For a family-friendly weekday happy hour with actual food options, this one's hard to argue with. 🍕

Happy hour is dine-in only, Mon–Fri 3–6PM. Not available for takeout or delivery.

post_title: Double Helix Wine Bar Happy Hour
post_content:
480 whiskeys and 50 wines by the glass — with a four-hour happy hour every single day. The Double Helix Wine & Whisky Lounge happy hour at Town Square runs daily 3:30–7:30pm with cocktails from $8.99, wine from $8, wells at $7.99, and a full food menu of small plates, tacos, sliders, and shareables all under $15. Order This:
  • Italiano Sliders ($12.99) — two award-winning Angus beef sliders with fried mozzarella, basil pesto, heirloom tomato, and balsamic reduction on brioche; the standout food item on the menu
  • Arancini ($10.99) — risotto fritters with mascarpone, roasted mushrooms, and truffle aioli; order these with a glass of Napa Cab ($9)
  • Lobster Tacos ($14.99) — beer-battered lobster, pico, chipotle sauce, grated cheese on soft corn tortillas; the splurge pick during the happy hour window
  • Old Fashioned ($9.99) — whiskey, bitters, demerara, rustic orange peel; well-executed, not overthought
  • Any bruschetta trio ($12.99) — choose any three from six options; the Prosciutto and Salmon are the move
A wine and whiskey lounge with a four-hour daily happy hour and 480 whiskeys on the shelf is not something most cities have — and this one is tucked into Town Square, which already has free parking and a walkable outdoor layout. All ages are welcome until 9pm, which makes it a genuinely flexible option for mixed groups. The food program is better than you'd expect from a drinks-first concept. The Italiano slider has won awards. Go before 7:30pm and order at least three things. 🥃 Daily 3:30–7:30pm. All ages until 9pm, 21+ after. Located at Town Square, 6599 S Las Vegas Blvd #150B.

Kabuki Japanese Restaurant in Town Square runs happy hour daily from 3 p.m. to close, and the lineup covers more ground than most: sushi and specialty rolls, small plates, cocktails, wine, and sake, all at reduced prices. Pair a couple rolls with a glass of sake and you've got a full meal without the full-price tab.

Town Square isn't the first place people think of for solid Japanese food, but Kabuki's been running this operation since 1991, and a daily-to-close happy hour is generous by Las Vegas standards — most spots cut it off well before dinner rush. That kind of consistency says something about who they're trying to keep coming back: locals near the 215, not tourists passing through. Worth putting on rotation if you're in that part of town.

No reservation needed for happy hour — just grab a seat at the bar or a table and order off the discounted menu until it ends for the night.

post_title: Lazy Dog Happy Hour Town Square
post_content: Regular happy hour prices at Lazy Dog dip low, and there's a second window at night when it happens again — this Town Square spot doesn't limit the deal to one lonely stretch of the afternoon. Order This: The chicken meatballs in spiced tomato curry sauce with a cooling cucumber drizzle stand out on a menu of $3–$8 bites, alongside chicken lettuce wraps, bacon candy, and brussels sprouts. Beers, bites, and signature cocktails all land in that same $3–$8 range, so a full round for two rarely breaks $20. This is the kind of happy hour that rewards knowing the schedule. Town Square isn't Strip-adjacent, so Lazy Dog leans into being a neighborhood spot with a cozy, lodge-inspired dining room — the deal here isn't built for tourists killing time, it's built for locals who'll actually come back twice in one week. Running the discount both in the afternoon and again late at night says something about who this place is trying to keep coming through the door. Happy hour runs Sunday through Friday, 3 to 6 p.m., with a reverse happy hour Monday through Thursday, 9 p.m. to midnight. Lazy Dog Happy Hour Summerlin Lazy Dog Happy Hour Henderson

post_title: Sickies Garage Burgers & Brews Happy Hour
post_content: Sickies Happy Hour Fifty beers, burgers that refuse to behave and a happy hour that runs daily. Sickies Garage Burgers & Brews in Town Square is the kind of place where “just one drink” can turn into a full-blown burger-and-beer situation. Sickies Happy Hour Menu with Prices The $10.99 Beer & a Burger combo is the smart play—a Garage Burger, choice of side and select domestic draft. You can also grab six boneless wings with fries for $8.99, while half-price pints and wine make the drink side easy. The happy hour at Sickies Garage runs Sunday through Friday from 3–6 p.m., plus Friday and Saturday from 9 p.m. to close. Half-price pints, half-price wine and discounted apps make this a useful stop before or after shopping at Town Square. The rotating beer list covers local craft, domestic and imports, so there’s plenty to explore. The garage-themed setting is unapologetically over the top, with automotive décor, big TVs and the kind of burger lineup that includes a doughnut-topped option. Recent reviews praise the generous portions, beer selection and casual atmosphere, though service can be hit or miss. Come hungry. Leave with your dignity—or at least the receipt.

post_title: Yard House Town Square Happy Hour
post_content:
The happy hour at Yard House Town Square runs Monday through Friday 3–6PM and again Sunday through Wednesday 10PM to close. Drinks are $2 off across the board, and select appetizers and pizzas are half off during the afternoon window.

Order This:

  • Poke Nachos — marinated ahi, crispy wontons, avocado, serranos, white truffle sauce, sweet soy ginger — half price during happy hour and the dish reviewers keep mentioning by name

Yard House Town Square reads like a faux-European outdoor mall, and Yard House fits right in — a beer hall posing as a casual American kitchen.

Town Square sits at the south end of Las Vegas Blvd — off the Strip, easy parking, outdoor mall energy that feels nothing like a casino. For the southwest valley crowd, it's the most accessible Yard House in the metro without committing to Summerlin or Henderson. The late-night Sun–Wed window is the underrated play here too: $2 off until close, no cover, no casino floor to navigate. 🍺

Happy hour runs Monday through Friday, 3 to 6 PM, with a late-night round Sunday through Wednesday from 10 PM until close. No reservations during happy hour — grab a seat at the bar.

post_content: Chef Daniel Marquez grew up eating this food in Mexico City, and it shows — the happy hour at Canonita doesn't feel like a hotel-restaurant afterthought, it feels like someone's actual heritage on a plate. That's not a gimmick tacked onto the food — Chef Marquez's menu holds up on its own, hand-pressed tortillas and all, so the view is a bonus rather than the whole pitch. It's a rare Strip happy hour where the setting and the cooking are both worth showing up for. Happy hour runs Monday through Thursday, 3-5 PM. *Note: This listing is not verified. The Rockhouse has not published updated information on a Happy Hour. If you plan to go, call ahead to confirm details. 702-731-9683

The Rockhouse Happy Hour

 It's called the 7-7-7 Happy hour because everything is $7

The Rockhouse is a sports bar, a dive bar, a rock 'n' roll bar, all rolled into one. It's a place where you can watch the game, belt out some karaoke, or just drown your sorrows in a cheap beer. And, miraculously, it's one of the best happy hour deals on the Strip.

Location & Hours

Located at The Grand Canal Shoppes inside The Venetian, 3377 South Las Vegas Blvd. Las Vegas, The Rockhouse Happy Hour runs Monday to Friday  2PM to 6PM.

 Happy Hour Menu and Prices

Now, don't expect fine dining or Michelin-star cuisine. The food here is solid bar fare, the kind that hits the spot after a few drinks. But for the price, it's hard to complain. And the drinks? Well, they're strong enough to knock you on your ass, which is exactly what you need after a long day of gambling and debauchery.

  • Appetizers $7
  • Draft beer $7
  • House wine $7
  • Well Cocktails $7

What is the Vibe at Rockhouse Happy Hour?

During Happy Hour, Rockhouse feels like a fun, no-frills hangout where you can kick back, grab cheap drinks and apps, play games, and soak in a carefree, rock-infused Las Vegas vibe.

Do I need a reservation for Rockhouse Happy Hour?

Many people just walk in — especially if you're headed for the bar during happy hour. Seating can fill up, so if it's important for you to have a spot (or you're in a group), calling ahead (702-731-9683) is a smart move. For more information please visit their website. (Rockhouse Las Vegas)

Conclusion

The Rockhouse is a breath of fresh air in the stuffy, over-priced world of Vegas. It's a place where you can let your hair down, have a good time, and not break the bank. So the next time you're in Sin City, skip the fancy restaurants and head to the Rockhouse. You won't be disappointed.

post_content: Six oysters for fifteen bucks, right on Restaurant Row, steps from the Sphere. Open kitchen, raw bar energy, a menu that swings from sushi rolls to bacon-wrapped dates without any pretense about it. The happy hour is the same idea shrunk down: no gimmicks, just the good stuff at bar prices, twice a day. That double window — afternoon and late night — means it works whether you're killing time before a show or looking for something to eat after one lets out. Happy hour runs Sunday through Thursday, 3-6pm and again 10pm to close, bar seating only. No reservations needed for the happy hour menu — walk up, sit down, order oysters.

post_content:
"Tanoshi" is Japanese for happy hour — and at Nobu Las Vegas inside Virgin Hotel, that one hour window is your most efficient entry point into one of the city's most recognized Japanese kitchens. The menu runs $6–$18 and the room is the same one that's been serving Black Cod with Miso since 1999. The Nobu Las Vegas Tanoshi Hour features signature cocktails with curated bar bites, available Sunday through Thursday from 6 to 7 PM in the lounge. Order This:
  • Yellowtail Jalapeño — the dish that defines Nobu's Japanese-Peruvian fusion style. Order it first.
  • Rock Shrimp Tempura — creamy spicy or ponzu. Reviewers consistently name it a standout.
  • Lychee Martini — the signature cocktail, and the one most people come back for.
  •  It's Not Me It's Yuzu — the other one worth trying if you're doing two drinks in an hour.
Nobu has been at this Las Vegas location since 1999, and the restaurant's following is a direct tribute to Chef Nobu Matsuhisa's approach to blending traditional Japanese cooking with Peruvian ingredients — a style he pioneered before it became a category. The Tanoshi Hour exists for exactly one reason: to give people who wouldn't otherwise drop $135 per person a seat at the table. It works. One hour, lounge seating, curated menu, same kitchen. If you've been meaning to try Nobu, this is how you do it without committing to the full dinner bill. 🍶 Sunday–Thursday, 6–7 PM, lounge only. Walk-ins welcome during Tanoshi Hour; reservations recommended for dinner.

Designer Todd Avery-Lenahan data-mined decades of old Strip photography to build this room, and it shows in every chandelier and banquette. Coming in late means the dinner crowd has thinned, the band is in full swing, and you're getting the full experience for the price of a few plates. Reservations recommended. 21+

$6 Asian-fusion street food bites inside one of Nevada's premier craft breweries — no casino floor, no slot machines, no smoke. The Arts District Kitchen happy hour runs Mon–Thu 3–6pm inside Able Baker Brewing on South Main Street, pairing discounted street food with the brewery's rotating craft beer lineup. Order This:

A $3 beer in Henderson, Monday through Friday, from 3 to 6. It's one of the cheapest pours in the Eastern Marketplace. 🍺 The happy hour at Chili's Henderson, at 10080 S. Eastern Ave, runs 3 to 6 p.m., Monday through Friday. It's a drinks-only deal: $3 for 16 oz Bud Light, Miller Lite, or Coors Light, $5 house wine, a $6 Margarita of the Month, and a $7 Tequila Classic Margarita. Order This: The Margarita of the Month at $6. It rotates, so ask what's in the shaker. The $3 16 oz domestics are the cheapest pour on the list.
  • $4: 22 oz Bud Light, Miller Lite, or Coors Light; 16 oz Modelo or Michelob Ultra
  • $5: 22 oz Modelo or Michelob Ultra; house red or white wine
This is a neighborhood happy hour for Henderson locals who want an easy, low-cost round after work. It's tucked into Eastern Marketplace, so parking's simple and there's no resort fee, valet line, or cover. The window is weekdays only and covers drinks, not food, so don't plan a weekend around it. Ask which cocktails qualify before you order, since specialty drinks may not. Show up around 3, sit at the bar, and start with the margarita of the month.   Other Chili's Grill & Bar Happy Hours: South Las Vegas Outlet Mall Craig Road Lake Mead & Rainbow North Decatur Rainbow – Arroyo Crossing Summerlin

post_title: Citrus Grill & Hookah Happy Hour Henderson
post_content:
Hookah served in a fresh orange or seasonal fruit bowl — alongside shawarma fries and $8 cocktails. The Citrus Grill & Hookah happy hour in Henderson runs Mon–Fri 4–7pm with discounted food, drinks, and the kind of low-key Mediterranean lounge atmosphere that's genuinely hard to find in this city. Order This:
  • Shawarma Fries — fries topped with your choice of chicken, steak, or gyro meat, feta cheese, ranch, and house hot sauce; the dish reviewers keep coming back to
  • Grass-Fed Signature Burger - ½ lb. blend of grass-fed chuck, brisket & short rib made juicy, rich, and full of flavor.
  • $8 cocktails (Mon–Fri 4–7pm) — well-priced for a full bar program with a rotating cocktail menu
  • Signature hookah in a fresh fruit bowl — served tableside; classic flavors and exotic blends available; ask about the hookah happy hour deal when you sit down
Citrus Grill is 21+ only, which sets the tone: this is a grown-up lounge that takes its food, hookah, and drink program seriously. The Henderson location on St. Rose Pkwy has a dog-friendly patio with heaters, an indoor lounge with comfy seating, and a staff that reviewers describe as genuinely attentive. In a neighborhood full of chain restaurants, this is the off-script option that Henderson locals treat as their own. The three-hour happy hour window gives you plenty of time to settle in and stay a while. 🍋 Happy hour Mon–Fri 4–7pm. Henderson location at 3440 St. Rose Pkwy, Suite 7. Open daily 11am–1am (2am Fri–Sat). 21+ only, valid ID required.

post_content: Downtown cocktail lounges don’t usually slow things down—but this one does it on purpose. Plush seating, dim lighting, and a crowd that actually settles in instead of rushing out. Classic Jewel,  located in the luxurious Juhl high rise in Downtown Las Vegas turns happy hour into a full unwind session, especially once the hookah starts flowing and the room shifts from bar to lounge. Happy hour here is built around cocktails, well drinks, and approachable bar bites meant for lingering. Prices rotate, but the focus stays on easy pours and shareable plates rather than overcomplicated mixology. Order This: a classic cocktail from the well, a couple of chilled beers or house pours, and a hookah session if you’re staying awhile. The hookah flavors are the real draw—smooth, aromatic, and meant for slow pacing rather than quick turnover. What sets it apart is the dual identity. Part cocktail lounge, part hookah lounge, it fills a niche Downtown that leans more social than party-heavy. You’re not here for a quick stop—you’re here because the night doesn’t need to speed up yet. It reflects a growing side of Las Vegas nightlife where conversation matters as much as the drink in your hand. Once you settle in, leaving early stops being the plan. The happy hour at Classic Jewel Downtown Las Vegas typically includes discounted drinks and select lounge offerings, with hookah available throughout the evening for those extending the night.

Plant-based fine dining on the Las Vegas Strip usually comes with a side of skepticism. Crossroads Kitchen Happy Hour shuts that down fast. This is not a “vegan option” restaurant—it’s fully plant-based fine dining in a space that still feels like a real night out on South Las Vegas Blvd, not a compromise. What is the happy hour at Crossroads Kitchen? It’s a vegan happy hour on the Las Vegas Strip featuring plant-based small plates, cocktails, and shareable bites from one of the city’s most polished meat-free kitchens. Crossroads happy hour menu with prices:
  • $10 CAVIAR AND CHIPS (GF) potato chips / French onion dip
  • $10 IMPOSSIBLE CIGARS spicy almond milk yogurt
  • $10 CALAMARI FRITTI (GF) diablo sauce / lemon
  • $10 CAESAR SALAD (GFO) choice of kale or romaine garlic focaccia croutons / Caesar dressing
The interesting part here isn’t just the food, it’s the placement. A fully plant-based fine dining restaurant sitting on South Las Vegas Blvd says a lot about where Vegas dining is going. This isn’t a wellness café tucked away in a plaza. It’s Strip-adjacent, polished, and confident enough to stand next to steakhouses and seafood towers. The crowd reflects that shift: locals who eat everything, curious tourists, and people who didn’t expect vegan food to taste like this. Show up early if you want a relaxed seat. Once word spreads through the casino corridor, it fills fast.

post_title: Downtown Terrace Kitchen & Bar Happy Hour
post_content:
There's an open rooftop patio at Downtown Container Park with a bird's-eye view of the 40-foot praying mantis and the Container Park stage — and the Downtown Terrace Kitchen & Bar happy hour runs there Mon-Fri 6–7 PM with discounted drinks and food specials on a seasonal farm-fresh menu. Las Vegas Advisor called it "below-the-radar" and noted it was packed with young locals in on the secret. Order This:
  • Quesadilla $13 - Mozzarella, Bell Peppers, Red Onion, Sour Cream
  • Steak Sandwich $19 -Arugula, tomato bruschetta, bacon, pesto aioli
  • Cocktails & Wines 1/2 off
Downtown Terrace sits on the second floor of a Container Park retail building, with an outdoor patio overlooking the common area. It's one of the only true rooftop happy hour spots in downtown Las Vegas with a real kitchen — not just a bar with a view. The menu leans light and seasonal, with farm-fresh dishes designed for sharing, which makes the daily Power Hour feel like a legitimate meal rather than a drink special with bar snacks. . 🌿 Walk-ins welcome; reservations available.

Ferraro's Happy Hour A Las Vegas restaurant that's been run by the same family since 1985, honored by Gambero Rosso with Tre Forchette in 2024 and named a Top Italian Restaurant three consecutive years, doing a daily happy hour with $10 meatballs and Carpaccio — that's Ferraro's Ristorante off the Strip, and "Ora Sociale" is exactly what it sounds like: a proper Italian social hour, not a discounted bar menu. Order This:
  • Polpette con Polenta at $10. Pork and beef meatballs over creamy cornmeal
  • Salsiccia con Fagioliat $12
  • Vitello Tonnato $16
The wine list has won Wine Spectator recognition, so order a glass with your small plates rather than defaulting to a cocktail. You're at a serious Italian restaurant, act accordingly. Ferraro's sits on Paradise Road, a block off the Strip. Executive Chef Mimmo Ferraro uses all-natural meats, hand-made pasta, and wild-caught fish prepared daily on-site which is what makes the happy hour price points feel like a gift rather than a loss leader. This is the rare off-Strip spot where you can eat like you're at dinner for the price of an appetizer round. Come before 7 PM and you've got one of the better deals in Las Vegas. Ora Sociale runs daily 4 to 7 PM in the bar, lounge, and patio areas. Must be 21+ to sit in the bar or lounge. Business casual dress code (leave the tank tops and flip-flops on the Strip).

(702)-982-8036 A 12-ounce New York strip for $29 during happy hour — at a speakeasy bar on West Sahara that regular customers recommend without reservation. The Herbs & Rye happy hour runs Mon–Sat 5–8pm with discounted menu items: steaks, seafood, cocktails, pasta, all of it. Order This:
  • 12oz New York Strip ($29 ) — the deal that built the reputation; half-price steak in a candlelit speakeasy is one of the best value propositions in Las Vegas dining
  • Filet Mignon  — perfectly cooked, $35 during happy hour; the dish reviewers single out as the highlight of the meal
  • Spicy Mussels ($22) / Littleneck Clams ($20) — the seafood option that balances the steak-heavy menu; order one for the table
  • Pre-Prohibition era cocktail — the menu is organized by historical eras; the bartenders know what they're doing; order from the Prohibition section first
Herbs & Rye looks like nothing from the outside — a strip mall on West Sahara, easy to drive past without noticing. Inside: burgundy red velvet walls, heavy oak booths, candlelight, and bartenders building hand-pressed juice cocktails with house-made bitters and serious precision. Industry workers and locals have packed the bar at 5pm since it opened. The happy hour runs until 8pm and the kitchen stays open until 3am, which makes it equally good for an early dinner and a late one. Go before 6pm if you want a seat without waiting. 🥃 Located at 3713 W Sahara Ave. Reservations recommended.

post_title: Hot N Juicy Crawfish Happy Hour Planet Hollywood
post_content:
Most Strip seafood boils are a tourist trap dressed in neon. The Hot N Juicy Crawfish inside Planet Hollywood is the exception — same menu, same prices, same Monday-through-Thursday happy hour as the local locations, just with a casino floor one escalator ride away. Order This:
  • Crawfish Étouffée during happy hour — the right introduction to the menu if you've never done a boil, or the right warmup if you have
  • Crawfish by the pound (live) gloves, bib, one sauce, one heat; the ritual is the same whether you're a local or just landed
  • Get Your Feet Wet combo crawfish, shrimp, andouille sausage, corn, and potatoes; the combo that converts first-timers into regulars
The happy hour at Hot N Juicy Crawfish Planet Hollywood offers discounted drinks and appetizers Monday through Thursday, 4–7 PM. The location inside the Miracle Mile Shops makes it accessible mid-Strip without the full casino-restaurant markup you'd expect. Parking validation is available through Planet Hollywood for the first hour. It's the same crawfish, the same sauce, the same mess — just with a different zip code. If you're staying nearby and want something that isn't a hotel restaurant, this is the move. 🦞 Walk-ins only. No reservations. post_title: Johnny Mac's Sports Bar & Grill Happy Hour Boulder Hwy
post_content:
Forty-three years on Boulder Highway and Johnny Mac's still draws the after-work crowd like clockwork. New York-style pizza, fresh never-frozen wings, and a sports bar that predates most of Henderson's zip codes — this is the original, and the happy hour keeps it relevant. The happy hour at Johnny Mac's Sports Bar & Grill on Boulder Highway in Henderson runs Monday through Friday, 3–6PM, with discounted drinks and a happy hour food menu built around the house specialties. This is a locals' institution, full stop. Brick walls, big TVs, booths worn in by decades of regulars — Johnny Mac's doesn't need to reinvent itself. The Boulder Hwy location at 842 S Boulder Hwy has the original-location energy; the Water St location is newer and runs the same deal. Ranked Top 100 US Restaurants of 2025 — and it's in a strip mall in Southern Highlands. The Prime 141 Steakhouse happy hour in Henderson runs twice daily in the lounge and bar, with $3.50 oysters, $7 steak sliders, $5.50 beer, $11 wine, and $15 craft cocktails from a kitchen with serious Strip pedigree. Order This:
  • Oysters ($3.50 each) — the happy hour anchor; fresh, cold, and a legitimate deal at a steakhouse of this caliber
  • Steak Sliders ($7 each) — the same kitchen execution as the full dining room, in a smaller format; order two
  • Seafood Cocktails ($4.50 each) — rotating selection, priced right, worth asking about when you sit down
  • Craft cocktail ($15) — the bar program is thoughtful and includes non-alcoholic options crafted with Lyre's spirits
Chef Tyler Frederick is a Las Vegas native who trained at the French Culinary Institute and worked at Le Cirque before opening Prime 141 in Southern Highlands — where he grew up. That context matters. This is a neighborhood steakhouse built by someone who actually knows the neighborhood, staffed by people with decades of Strip experience, operating without the Strip markup. Food media has noticed: one reviewer called the happy hour practically a public service. The automatic 22% gratuity is worth knowing about upfront — it's shared across front and back of house — but the food and service justify it. 🥩 Happy hour is twice daily 3-5:30pm & 9-10 pm week days, 9-11 Sat-Sun. Reservations recommended for dinner. Located at 10670 Southern Highlands Pkwy, Suite 101.   “GIGGLE JUICE FREE” The choice not to drink is different for everyone. Our cocktail program is committed to a responsible drinking culture. The noted cocktails are available “GIGGLE JUICE FREE” crafted with Lyre’s alcohol-free spirits.

Rainforest Cafe Happy Hour 

The Rainforest Cafe offers a unique dining experience that transports guests into a tropical paradise. Beyond its immersive ambiance, the cafe's Happy Hour stands out as a delightful retreat for both locals and tourists seeking a blend of exotic surroundings and delectable offerings.

Location

Located within the Miracle Mile Shops in Las Vegas 3717 South Las Vegas Blvd.

What is the Vibe at Rainforest Cafe?

From the moment you step inside, you're enveloped by the sights and sounds of a lush rainforest. The decor features cascading waterfalls, dense vegetation, and animatronic wildlife, creating an atmosphere that appeals to all ages. This immersive setting makes it more than just a meal—it's an adventure. Happy Hour Details Rainforest Cafe's Happy Hour is available Monday through Friday from 2:00 PM to 6:00 PM, exclusively in the bar area. This time frame offers an excellent opportunity to unwind after a day of shopping or exploring Las Vegas. Appetizer Highlights The Happy Hour menu features a selection of appetizers priced at $8 each, including:
  • Spinach Dip: A creamy blend of spinach and cheeses, served with crispy tortilla chips.
  • Chicken Quesadillas: Grilled tortillas filled with seasoned chicken and melted cheese, accompanied by salsa and sour cream.
  • Cheese Sticks: Golden-fried mozzarella sticks paired with marinara dipping sauce.
These offerings provide a satisfying start to the evening, allowing guests to sample a variety of flavors without committing to a full meal. Beverage Specials Complementing the appetizers, the beverage specials include:
  • $4 Beers: A selection of domestic and imported brews.
  • $5 Well Drinks: Classic mixed drinks crafted with well liquors.
  • $6 Cocktails: Specialty cocktails that vary, offering a taste of the tropics.
These drink specials cater to a wide range of preferences, ensuring that every guest finds something to enjoy.

Guest Experiences

Patrons frequently praise the Happy Hour offerings at Rainforest Cafe. One reviewer highlighted the engaging service provided by the bartender. Such testimonials reflect the cafe's commitment to providing both value and a memorable experience.

Conclusion

The Rainforest Cafe at Miracle Mile Shops offers a Happy Hour that combines enticing food and drink specials with an unparalleled atmosphere. Whether you're seeking a brief escape from the desert heat or a unique spot to gather with friends, this tropical oasis provides a refreshing retreat in the heart of Las Vegas.

$4 wine and $5 risotto at a sit-down Italian restaurant — every weekday, no reservations required. The Romano's Macaroni Grill happy hour runs Mon–Fri 3–7pm with a dedicated bar menu featuring $5 appetizers, $7 cocktails, and $4 house wine that reviewers consistently call one of the better deals in the neighborhood. Order This:
  • Cacio e Pepe Arancini ($5) — crispy fried risotto balls with romano and black pepper; the happy hour snack that punches well above its price point
  • Mushroom Risotto ($5) — a full-portion starter at bar prices; order it first
  • Calamari Fritti ($9) — crispy calamari with calabrian pepper pesto and citrus black pepper aioli; the table appetizer that disappears fastest
  • Blood Orange Cosmo, Espresso Martini, or Italian Margarita Prima ($7 each) — the cocktail menu is better than you'd expect from a chain
  • House wine ($4 per glass) — the whole reason regulars show up at 3pm
The happy hour is Monday-Friday, which matters. Wine-by-the-glass at $4, craft-adjacent cocktails at $7, and a rotating appetizer menu built around imported Italian ingredients make this one of the more reliable weekday value plays in the city. Reviewers call out the bar area specifically as cozy and well-run. If you've written off the chain, the happy hour is a decent reason to reconsider. 🍷 Mon–Fri 3–7pm. Bar seating, no reservation needed.

post_content: Half-price 16 oz. drafts and $2 off wells at a 24-hour neighborhood bar that's open when nothing else is — Scoundrels Pub II on Camino Al Norte is the kind of North Las Vegas spot that doesn't need to advertise because the regulars just keep showing up. The happy hour at Scoundrels Pub II runs Monday through Friday, 3 to 6 PM, with 50% off 16 oz. draft beer and $2 off well cocktails and wine. Order This: $1 crispy chicken wings, $7 loaded fries, and $4 queso — bar food that hits right during the 3 PM lull. The wing price especially is hard to argue with. Pair with a half-price draft and you've got a full happy hour spread for under $15. Scoundrels Pub II is open 24 hours, which already separates it from most of the competition — but the happy hour is where the neighborhood crowd actually congregates. Pool tables, a lounge area away from the main bar, and a kitchen that doesn't close make this the kind of place where you stop in for one drink and end up staying. North Las Vegas doesn't have a long list of reliable after-work bars, which is exactly why this one has regulars who treat it like their living room. Come on a weekday and you'll understand immediately. Happy hour is Monday through Friday, 3 to 6 PM. No reservation, no dress code, no pretense — walk in and find a stool.

post_content:
Sea bass taqueria and short rib tostaditas at a Wine Spectator Award-winning Mexican steakhouse — with a happy hour menu that makes the Strip's most dramatic room accessible. The Toca Madera happy hour at The Shops at Crystals runs Mon-Fri–4-6pm- the bar only, with discounted cocktails, beer, and a focused food menu built from the same organic and sustainable ingredients as the full dinner service. Order This:
  • Short Rib Tostaditas ($12) — three per order; rich, generous, and the item Las Vegas Advisor described as "so plentiful we couldn't finish them"; order these first

Toca Madera is the Noble 33 group's Las Vegas flagship, tucked into the courtyard between Aria and The Shops at Crystals — a location that's easy to miss if you don't know to look for the unmarked door. The happy hour is how you sit in that room for $30–$40 instead of $100+. Dress accordingly. Mon–Fri 4–6pm. Bar only. post_content:
50% off selected items daily 2–4pm at a Gordon Ramsay restaurant inside Caesars Palace — and no reservation required at the bar. The Gordon Ramsay Pub & Grill happy hour at Caesars Palace is one of the more straightforward Strip deals: show up between 2 and 4pm, order half-price chef-inspired appetizers and discounted cocktails, and sit in a 290-seat British pub with 36 beers on tap and British telephone booths as the backdrop. Order This:
  • Pigs in a Blanket
  • Maple-Glazed Bacon
  • Any of 36 beers on tap — Boddingtons, Newcastle, Guinness, Samuel Adams, Anchor Steam, and more; the tap list is the pub's strongest argument
The happy hour runs daily 2–4pm with 50% off selected items — which makes it one of the few Strip restaurants offering a genuine midday discount window rather than the standard 4–6pm setup. The 290-seat venue is two restaurants in one, with a bar centered around British telephone booths and a patio that extends toward the casino floor. The Pigs in a Blanket earn high marks, as does the Maple-Glazed Bacon — both at half price. Located near the Forum Shops and the Colosseum, it's well-positioned for a pre-show stop. Go at 2pm, order the Smoked Cheddar & Spinach Dip and decide the rest from there. Daily 2–4pm, 50% off selected items. No dress code. Reservations recommended for dinner but not required at the bar. Located at Caesars Palace, 3570 S Las Vegas Blvd.

Three price tiers, zero decision fatigue — Benihana's happy hour at Fashion Show Mall breaks everything down to $3, $6, or $9, so you can build a full spread without doing math at the table. Order This:

The sushi bar and lounge become the move here — teppanyaki tables aren't part of the happy hour, but you don't need the flaming-onion show to get a solid meal. Benihana sits on the second level of Fashion Show Mall, right across from Wynn and Encore, which makes it an easy landing spot mid-shopping-trip or before a Strip show without needing a car or a cab. It's proof that a 60-year-old chain can still run a genuinely useful discount window on some of the busiest real estate in town. Happy Hour runs Monday through Friday, 3 to 6 p.m., dine-in only at the sushi bar and lounge. Not available on holidays or with other promotions. Benihana Happy Hour Westgate Las Vegas

Galpão Gaucho Brazilian Steakhouse Happy Hour

Galpão Gaucho Brazilian Steakhouse Happy Hour at Fashion Show Mall is in one of Las Vegas’s premier shopping and entertainment destinations. It is an experience that transports guests straight to the heart of Brazil with its rich culinary traditions and vibrant atmosphere. Celebrating the art of churrasco, this happy hour offers a delightful array of discounted drinks and flavorful dishes that showcase the best of authentic Brazilian cuisine.

Location & Hours

Galpão Gaucho Brazilian Steakhouse is located on the second floor at the entrance to the Fashion Show Mall at 3200 South Las Vegas Blvd. Happy Hour is offered Monday through Friday 4 PM to 7 PM and Saturday and Sunday 3 PM to 6 PM at the Bar or High Top Tables.

Is there a dress code at Galpão Gaucho Happy Hour?

Yes — Galpão Gaucho Brazilian Steakhouse lists a business casual dress code. So for Happy Hour, you’ll want to lean toward smart-casual: nice jeans or slacks, a collared shirt or a clean top, and appropriate shoes.

Happy Hour Menu and Prices

The culinary offerings during happy hour are enticing. The menu is a celebration of authentic Brazilian fare, designed to highlight the natural flavors of high-quality ingredients.
  • Shrimp Grelhado $19
  • Grilled Salmon $24
  • Picanha (Prime Sirloin) $18
  • Lamb Chops $28
  • Charcuterie Board $21

Happy Hour Drinks

At the heart of the happy hour experience is the drink menu, which offers an impressive selection of cocktails and beverages that pay tribute to Brazilian flavors. The happy hour specials also include a carefully curated selection of beers, ranging from local craft brews to international favorites, as well as a fine assortment of wines chosen to complement the diverse happy hour menu.
  • Hand Crafted Cocktails $6 - $8
  • Wine by the Glass $7 - $8
  • Draft Beer $5

What is the Vibe at Galpão Gaucho Happy Hour?

Upon entering Galpão Gaucho, guests are immediately struck by the warm and inviting ambiance that permeates the space. The decor is a tasteful blend of rustic Brazilian charm and modern elegance, with earthy tones, wooden accents, and subtle nods to the country’s cultural heritage. The atmosphere is lively yet relaxed, inviting patrons to settle in comfortably as they prepare to enjoy an evening of good food, great drinks, and engaging conversation. It is this perfect balance of energy and relaxation that makes Galpão Gaucho an ideal spot for happy hour.

Do I need to make a reservation for Galpão Gaucho Happy Hour?

Because happy hour is limited to the bar area, you may not need a reservation. However, if your group is bigger, you should make one to be safe. For more information please visit their website or phone (702) 602-0384.

Final thoughts

The experience at Galpão Gaucho’s happy hour is not just about great food and drinks; it is also a celebration of Brazilian culture and culinary traditions. The restaurant has managed to capture the essence of Brazil, from the lively flavors of its cocktails to the robust, smoky notes of its grilled meats. This cultural authenticity, combined with modern touches and an inviting atmosphere, makes Galpão Gaucho a standout destination for anyone looking to enjoy a truly immersive happy hour experience.

José Andrés calls his happy hour "Sangría Hour" — and at Jaleo inside the Cosmopolitan, that distinction actually means something. This is one of the few Strip restaurant happy hours where you're eating tapas from a James Beard Award-winning chef's kitchen at prices that don't require a second mortgage. The Jaleo Sangría Hour runs Sunday–Thursday 5–7 PM and Friday–Saturday 4:30–7 PM, in the bar and lounge, with signature tapas, iconic sangrías, and wines and beer by the glass. There's also a Reverse Sangría Hour Monday 9–11 PM. Order This:

  • Croquetas de Pollo — $7 — traditional chicken fritters. The one item regulars order every single visit.
  • Gazpacho Estilo Algeciras — $4 — The smartest $4 you'll spend on the Strip.
  • Bottle & Board — $68 --a bottle of red, white, or sparkling wine paired with specialty Spanish cheeses and cured Ibérico meats. The move for two people.
  • Cocktails — $13 | Wine — $10
The Paella Grill is one of only three open-fire wood paella grills of its kind in the world, which explains why the room feels like theater as much as a restaurant. It feels like sitting at a street side café in Madrid — on the third floor of the Cosmopolitan. The Sangría Hour is the entry point. Most people who go once end up back for dinner. 🥂

Leticia's Cocina & Cantina brings genuinely scratch-made Mexican cooking to a neighborhood casino setting, with a "Viva Happy Hour" menu that actually earns the name. The Leticia's Cocina & Cantina happy hour runs Monday–Friday 3–5 PM at Santa Fe Station, with $6 draft beers, $6 well drinks, and $9 house margaritas. The small eats menu is where the real value is. Order This:
  • ChangiBirria — $9 — flour tortilla, beans, cheese, and beef birria fried crispy, served with consommé for dipping. The standout item on this menu.
  • Taquitos Enchilados — $9 — three crispy taquitos with your choice of filling (chicken tinga, beef, carnitas, potato & cheese) in ranchera, verde, mole, or diabla sauce. With lettuce, guac, pico, crema, and queso cotija.
  • Smoked Tacos — $10 — two smoked strip steak tacos, caramelized onions, jalapeños, guacamole. These are the splurge.
  • Empanaditas — $9 — two crispy corn masa, shrimp and chorizo or rajas con queso, finished with crema and queso cotija.
No canned goods, no shortcuts — that's been the rule here since day one. The happy hour menu at Leticia's Santa Fe reads like a condensed version of the full kitchen's capability: birria, smoked steak, housemade sauces, fresh masa. Northwest Vegas has a legitimate Mexican food scene and Leticia's has been anchoring it for over 15 years. Make it a weekday habit. 🌮 Monday–Friday, 3–5 PM. Walk-ins welcome. Fiorella

Fiorella Happy Hour – A Taste of Italy in Summerlin

If you're looking to wind down in style and soak in a little Italian flair, Fiorella in the Durango Hotel & Casino in Summerlin has just the thing—Aperitivo Hour, their version of Happy Hour that channels the warm, easygoing vibes of Italy. This isn’t your average Happy Hour with greasy bar food and watered-down drinks. At Fiorella, they do things the Italian way. Aperitivo Hour is all about enjoying light bites and flavorful drinks in good company—perfect for catching up with friends, unwinding after work, or easing into your evening plans.

On the drink side, expect a classy lineup that includes Italian staples like the bold and bitter Negroni, the crisp and bubbly Aperol Spritz, and other refreshing Campari-based cocktails. These are the kinds of drinks that don’t just quench your thirst—they spark conversation and get you into that laid-back, sunset state of mind. What makes it even better? Fiorella pairs their cocktails with complimentary small bites. We’re talking olives, bruschetta, maybe some creamy cheese and charcuterie. These aren’t full meals, but they’re just enough to nibble on while you sip and socialize. The idea is to stimulate your appetite without spoiling dinner—and it works like a charm. The vibe at Fiorella is casual, comfortable, and inviting—ideal for a pre-dinner gathering or even a light, early evening hang. You won’t feel rushed here; it’s all about enjoying the moment, the company, and the taste of something special. Aperitivo Hour isn’t just a promo—it’s a cultural experience. In Italy, it’s a daily ritual. And Fiorella brings that same energy to Summerlin, blending tradition with a modern twist that feels just right for locals who love good food and great drinks without the fuss. Whether you’re already a fan of European-style Happy Hours or you’re just looking to switch up your usual routine, Fiorella’s Aperitivo Hour is a refreshing change of pace. Bring your friends, bring your appetite, and get ready to toast to a little slice of Italy right here in Summerlin. post_title: Juan's Flaming Fajitas Happy Hour Centennial
post_content:
They light the fajitas on fire at the table. That's not a gimmick — it's been Juan's signature move since day one, and it's part of why this locally owned Mexican restaurant has been voted Best Mexican Food in Las Vegas across multiple years.

The happy hour at Juan's Flaming Fajitas in the Centennial area runs daily 3–6PM, restaurant-wide — not just bar seating — with discounted appetizers and drink specials. The Cadillac Margarita with your choice of tequila is the drink to order.

  • Queso Fundido — sizzling skillet, mixed monterey and cheddar, pico de gallo, dual salsas
  • Tableside Guacamole — made fresh, order it first
  • Sopapillas to finish — reviewers keep mentioning them

Specific happy hour appetizer and drink pricing isn't posted publicly — ask your server when you sit down.

At 2660 W. Centennial Pkwy in North Las Vegas, this location draws the northwest corridor crowd that knows Juan's from years of repeat visits. The 4.6-star Yelp rating across 1,300+ reviews doesn't happen by accident. Restaurant-wide happy hour means you can bring the family, grab a real table, and order the full experience — not just bar snacks. 🌶️

The smart play here is grabbing a seat in the lounge while the piano is going. It feels old Vegas, just in Henderson. Hank’s has been one of Green Valley Ranch’s anchor dining spots for years, and the happy hour exists for people who want the steakhouse feel without the full steakhouse bill. Get there early—bar seats go fast, especially on weekends.

Stubborn Seed has retained its Michelin star for three consecutive years, and recent diners continue to praise the food, service and creative dishes. Come early, order a few plates and see how much Michelin-starred technique you can get for the price of a couple Strip cocktails.

post_content: A $1.99 margarita at 3am is not a typo — it's just Tuesday at Santa Fe Station. 4949 Lounge runs happy hour twice a day, and the second one lands deep in reverse-happy-hour territory, when the rest of the city has already gone to bed. Few places in the valley will sell you a shot and a $2 margarita after your shift ends at 3am, and that's reason enough to know this one exists. Happy hour runs daily 5-7pm, plus a reverse happy hour from 2-6am. No reservation needed — just walk up to the bar.

Dom DeMarco’s offers two tiers to their Monday through Friday Happy Hour:
  1. From 2 to 6 PM, you can get in on their regular Happy Hour
  2. Between 2 and 4 PM, you’ll experience what they proudly call their “Happiest of Happy Hours.”
Two tiers of happy hour at the same spot is unusual. 50% off all pizzas during the earlier window is almost unheard of. Dom DeMarco's in Summerlin runs one of the most generous happy hour setups in Las Vegas, and the lineage behind the pizza makes it worth understanding before you order. Order This: from 2–4 PM, all pizzas are 50% off — this is the window to go, full stop. Clock out early and get a thick-crust eggplant or white truffle pie at half price on the patio. From 2–6 PM, the $12 food menu kicks in alongside 50% off well drinks and select wines by the glass and bottle, plus $3 off select beers. If you miss the pizza discount, the drink deal still holds — you just pay full price for the pie. Dom DeMarco's carries the torch of Di Fara Pizza in Brooklyn, where the original Dom DeMarco spent over five decades making pies by hand on Avenue J. The Las Vegas location has been voted Best Pizza and Best Happy Hour by the Las Vegas Review-Journal — not just once, but multiple years running. Summerlin has no shortage of Italian options, but very few with this kind of origin story behind them. Show up before 4 PM on a weekday and you'll eat like the deal was made for regulars, because it was. Happy hour runs Monday through Friday, 2–6 PM, with the "Happiest of Happy Hours" — 50% off all pizzas — from 2–4 PM only. Sit on the patio if the weather cooperates. No reservation needed.

It's trying to be reliable, and it succeeds. Come in before 5 PM and you'll have your pick of bar seats. Happy hour runs daily 4to 6 PM, in the bar area only. Award-winning craft beer brewed on the premises — and a non-smoking taproom in Summerlin where you can actually taste it. The Chicago Brewing Company happy hour runs Mon–Fri 3–6pm and 11 pm-1 am with 50% off all pints, discounted appetizers, and a rotating tap list that has won medals at both the Great American Beer Festival and The World Beer Cup. Order This:

Just award-winning beer brewed on site and a bar that knows what it's doing. The Great American Beer Festival medals on the wall aren't decoration; they reflect a brewery that's been competing at the national level for decades. If your default after-work spot has a smoky gaming bar attached to it, this is the upgrade you've been putting off. 🍺 Mon–Fri 3–6pm and 11pm-1am. Located at 2201 S Fort Apache Rd, Suite 110. $4 steak and eggs and $3 top-shelf cocktails — at an award-winning butcher shop and steakhouse in Tivoli Village. The Echo & Rig happy hour at the Summerlin flagship runs Mon–Fri 3–6pm with some of the most specific and well-priced bar bites of any off-Strip steakhouse in Las Vegas. Order This:
  • Steak & Egg ($4) — prime steak, sunny side up egg; the happy hour item reviewers call out by name every single time; order it immediately
  • Butcher Fries ($5) — Kennebec fries topped with prime steak and house-made sauce; the loaded fries that justify the drive to Tivoli Village on their own
  • Hot Dog ($3) — sauerkraut, brown mustard; a $3 hot dog at a steakhouse is a deliberate choice that works completely
  • $3 top-shelf cocktails — the bar program at Echo & Rig is serious; order something from the craft cocktail list and let the bartender make the call
Chef Sam Marvin — creator of Bottega Louie in Los Angeles — built Echo & Rig around a single idea: put the butcher shop front and center, let the customer see the cuts, and price the happy hour in a way that gets people in the door without cheapening the experience. The Tivoli Village flagship is where the concept began, and the on-site butcher shop means everything served at the bar during happy hour starts with the same sourcing as the $60 dinner entrees. The Summerlin crowd that has been coming here since it opened treats the 3–6pm window as a standing reservation. Complimentary valet from Tivoli Village makes the logistics easy. 🥩 Located at 440 S Rampart Blvd, Tivoli Village. Reservations recommended for dinner: (702) 489-3525. Echo & Rig Henderson also offers exceptional happy hour experience but in a different way. Check out the Echo & Rig Happy Hour Henderson menu and make it a must-see happy hour next time you're in Henderson.

Swans on a lake, 950-label wine shop, half-price wine by the glass, and escargot for $12 — ten miles from the Strip in a quiet residential neighborhood. The Marché Bacchus happy hour in Summerlin runs daily 2–5pm in the bar area with 50% off wines by the glass, specialty cocktails from $6, and a focused French bistro bar menu that's genuinely hard to beat at these prices. Order This:
  • Escargot ($12) — garlic, parsley butter, the French bistro classic; order it first and order it every time
  • Bacchus Bacon Burger ($24) — 8oz Angus beef, in-house baked truffle brioche, Gruyère, bacon, caramelized onions, parsley-garlic aioli; the bar burger that earns the price
  • Artichoke Beignets ($12) — basil, lime aioli; the vegetable option that converts skeptics
  • Elderflower Gin & Tonic ($7) — Empress Gin, Limoncello, Fever Tree Elderflower Tonic, fresh rosemary; the cocktail that fits the setting perfectly
  • Any wine by the glass (50% off) — choose from the on-site retail wine shop at retail price plus a $10 corkage fee; over 950 labels available
Awarded Best Vegas Outdoor Restaurant, Best French, and listed in the Top 10 of "Eating Las Vegas: The 50 Essential Restaurants," Marché Bacchus has been earning its reputation since 2000. The recent acquisition by HUKL Hospitality in late 2024 brought new energy while keeping the kitchen's French bistro foundation intact. Sitting on the lakeside patio watching the swans drift by with a half-price glass of Burgundy costs less than most Strip cocktails. That's not a metaphor — it's just what happens here every afternoon. 🦢 Daily 2–5pm, bar area only. Open Mon–Sun 11am–9pm. Located at 2620 Regatta Dr, Suite 106, in the Desert Shores community near Summerlin. Patio reservations recommended — the lakeside tables book fast on weekends.

It's the kind of place that doesn't need to try hard to fill seats at 4 PM on a Tuesday. Walk in, grab a bar stool, and let the meatballs do the convincing. Happy hour at Osteria Fiorella runs Wednesday, Thursday and Sunday from 4:30 to 6 PM at Red Rock Casino, and it's one of the few deals in Summerlin where the discount touches food cooked by an actual James Beard winner, not just the bar menu. Wine pours run generous, per regulars, so don't be shy about ordering a glass instead of a cocktail. Marc Vetri built his name on Philly's Fiorella before bringing an expanded version to Summerlin, and the Red Rock setting means you get a casual, warm atmosphere with a lively bar, a patio, and an open kitchen instead of Strip-level pretension. It's a locals' casino doing a chef-driven Italian happy hour right, which is the kind of thing Summerlin regulars know and Strip tourists never find. Go on a Wednesday before it gets busy. Happy hour is Wednesday, Thursday and Sunday, 4:30–6 PM, at the bar and patio. No ticket required — just show up and grab a seat before the regulars do.

post_title: Rustic House Happy Hour Boca Park
post_content:
Two happy hours a day sounds like a typo, but Rustic House in Summerlin actually runs one from 4-6 PM and a second overnight from 12 AM to 6 AM — because someone finally remembered graveyard shift workers drink too. Order This: The Nachos drop down to 50% off during happy hour.  Pair them with $5 beers or $6 well drinks, and if you're rolling through after 9 PM, every drink in the house is 50% off until sunrise. This is a family-friendly, non-smoking gaming bar, which is its own kind of rare in Vegas — you can watch the game, feed the kids, and still catch a deal without walking into a smoke cloud. The projectors inside and out mean the patio watches the same broadcast as the bar, so there's no reason to fight for a TV seat. Between the two happy hour windows, there's almost no time of day Rustic House isn't running a deal. Rustic House's happy hour runs daily 4-6 PM with 50% off appetizers, $5 beers, $6 well drinks, and $7 wines, plus a second overnight happy hour from 9 PM to 7 AM offering 50% off all drinks. Located in Boca Park, Summerlin, with seating at the bar, lounge, and patio.

Siena will be closed on Mondays from June 8, 2026, through September 14, 2026.

A "Reverse Happy Hour" that kicks in at 9 PM Tues-Wed — that's not something you see at most Italian spots, and it's the kind of detail that separates Siena from every other trattoria in Summerlin. Order This: The Meatball & Mozzarella at $9 is the easy starter, but if you're settling in, the Calamari Fritti at $15 with spicy marinara is the one worth ordering for the table. Add the Cheese Pizza at $12 and you've got a full happy hour spread that doesn't feel like a compromise on quality. Siena started as an east-side Italian deli back in the 1970s before this Summerlin trattoria opened, and Chef Giancarlo Bomparola — Milan-raised — runs the kitchen with real northern Italian technique instead of red-sauce shortcuts. That history matters here: this isn't a concept restaurant chasing a trend, it's a family business that earned its regulars the slow way. With happy hour running daily and a second discount window after 9 PM, there's rarely a bad time to swing by the lounge next door. Happy hour runs daily 2:30-6:30PM, with a second "Reverse Happy Hour" Tues-Wed from 9-10PM and 3-9PM Sunday at the bar only. Located at 9500 W Sahara Ave, Summerlin.

The Spy Ninjas HQ happy hour at the Retro Bar + Arcade is genuinely one of the more unexpected happy hours in Las Vegas, and it works precisely because it's not trying to be a traditional bar. Foundation Room Happy Hour

Happy Hour at the Foundation Room is offered Monday through Thursday starting at 5 p.m. and Sundays at 6 PM

What truly distinguishes the Foundation Room Happy Hour from other lounges is its rooftop terrace, which offers one of the best panoramic views in the city on the 63rd Floor at Mandalay Bay.

Perched atop Mandalay Bay, the Foundation Room offers one of the most sophisticated and visually arresting Happy Hour experiences in Las Vegas. This exclusive lounge, known for its opulent décor and elevated ambiance, transforms the typical post-work gathering into a high-style ritual. With a rooftop patio that boasts sweeping views of the Las Vegas Strip and an interior reminiscent of a regal Eastern palace, the Foundation Room blends elegance with a touch of mysticism—making Happy Hour here as much about the atmosphere as it is about the offerings.

The Foundation Room Happy Hour Menu with Prices

Happy Hour at the Foundation Room is offered Monday through Thursday starting at 5 p.m. and Sundays at 6 PM. During this coveted time, guests can enjoy an elevated happy hour menu of libations and small plates that reflect the lounge’s refined aesthetic. Spirits are priced at $11 and include premium selections like New Amsterdam Vodka, Bacardi Rum, Beefeater Gin, and more. Wine lovers can sip on varietals by the glass for $9, with options such as Riesling, Pinot Grigio, Pinot Noir, and Merlot. For beer enthusiasts, a curated list featuring Corona, Heineken, Stella Artois, Budweiser, Michelob Ultra, and others is available for $7. Complementing the drinks are globally inspired bites like Vindaloo Tacos ($13), featuring curry and tamarind-braised chicken with mint yogurt, Chicken Pintxos ($11) topped with bold red chimichurri, and Cauliflower Tempura ($10). What truly distinguishes the Foundation Room happy hour from other lounges is the rooftop Happy hour on the 63rd floor, which offers one of the best views of the Vegas Strip.

Happy Hour Expert Advice for the Foundation Room

The rooftop happy hour during the summer months is hot and bright. The best time to visit the Foundation Room to enjoy the rooftop happy hour is from Sep to May with more comfortable temperatures and a glittery view of the neon strip. Foundation Room elevators are on the opposite side of the resort as the convention center and restaurant row. Look for Hazel Coffee & Cocktails and the elevator are around the corner and up...way up! In a city where Happy Hour options are abundant, the Foundation Room distinguishes itself by offering not just discounted drinks, but a complete sensory experience—elevated, exclusive, and utterly unforgettable. For those seeking a touch of refinement with their revelry, this rooftop escape is a must-visit.

The Foundation Room Happy Hour

The Foundation room Happy hour is great for conferences at Mandalay Bay who need a break and fresh air from the conference floor. The menu is good as is the cocktail and wine selection and price. If you want to impress clients or a team get together, the Foundation room Happy hour will work well. I recommend The Foundation Room Happy hour for conference goers and visitors who want a different perspective of the Strip...63 floors up. :)

post_content:
More than 100 beers on tap, half-price apps, and $2 off everything you drink — Yard House at Sunset Station is the rare happy hour where the beer list alone is worth the drive. It's right next to the Sunset Sportsbook & Bar, with the largest selection of draft beer paired with a diverse menu inspired by California roots, so good luck finding a seat during March Madness.

Order This:

  • Poke Nachos — marinated ahi, crispy wontons, avocado, serranos, white truffle sauce, sweet soy ginger — half price during happy hour and the dish reviewers keep mentioning by name
  • Boneless Wings — half off, choose from Buffalo, Korean Chili Garlic, or Nashville Hot

  • Chicken Lettuce Wraps and Sliders — both half off

Henderson doesn't need Strip flash — it needs a place with a beer list deep enough to argue about and a happy hour that doesn't punish you for showing up after work. This Sunset Station location is large, runs an online wait list, and has plenty of TVs for whatever game's on, which is exactly what a casino sports bar should be. It's the kind of happy hour locals build a routine around, not a one-off. Happy hour runs Monday through Friday, 3 to 6 PM, with a late-night round Sunday through Wednesday from 10 PM until close. No reservations during happy hour — grab a seat at the bar.

Everything's six bucks — that's the entire happy hour math at Arts District Kitchen's happy hour, no fine print, no tiered pricing, just pick a beer and pick a basket. Arts District Kitchen's happy hour runs Monday through Thursday, 3-6pm, inside Able Baker Brewing, with five house drafts and five snacks all priced at $6 flat. Order This:
  • A pint of Atomic Duck, Able Baker's flagship IPA, alongside the onion rings — reviewers call them "BOMB," and for $6 they're not wrong
  • Enchilada chips or Nashville hot fries if you want the kitchen's Southeast Asian-leaning street food angle instead of standard bar snacks
  • Split Bill, Mango Drop, or El Pato Loco if you're working through the draft list one $6 pint at a time
Arts District Kitchen operates inside the taproom, a genuine collaboration rather than a food truck bolted onto a brewery, and it's why the menu goes beyond pretzels into banh mi, fish tacos, and craft burgers once happy hour ends. Able Baker itself takes its name from the first two atomic bomb tests at the Nevada Test Site — a very Vegas piece of trivia for a very Downtown brewery. This is the Arts District doing what it does best: no casino floor, no slot machine noise, just a community taproom where locals actually want to sit for a while. No reservations, dog-friendly patio when the heat allows it — walk in, grab a table, and don't overthink the menu. Everything's the same price anyway.

Fremont Street gets loud, but Hennessey’s Tavern Happy Hour is where you actually catch your breath. This Irish pub sits right in the middle of the chaos, yet somehow keeps a steady flow of locals, bartenders off-shift, and people who know better than to overpay for drinks on Fremont. What is the happy hour at Hennessey’s Tavern? It’s a Fremont Street Irish pub happy hour with discounted drinks, classic bar bites, and live music in a casual, no-frills setting right in downtown Las Vegas. Order This:
  • Korean BBQ Chicken Bite - breaded chicken glazed with Korean BBQ sauce topped with sesame & green onion
  • Crispy Fried Pickle Spear - with Ranch dipping sauce
  • Seared Ahi Tacos - ahi seared rare topped with sriracha slaw
  •  Guinness or local draft — this is still an Irish pub, after all.
The real hook here isn’t just the prices—it’s the location. Fremont Street is built for sensory overload, and Hennessey’s gives you a rare pocket where you can sit, eat, and still watch the madness without being swallowed by it. Live music spills out onto the street most nights, which means your happy hour can easily turn into a full Fremont session without you planning it. This is the kind of place you end up at “for one drink” and leave two hours later wondering what happened. Grab a seat early if you want a good view of the street performers.

Gaetano's in Henderson still runs one of the most generous happy hours in the valley. This is the kind of place where the meatballs are made with filet mignon, veal, and pork, and the happy hour still prices them at $10 for two. The Gaetano's happy hour runs daily 4–6 PM in the bar, with bar bites and cocktails purpose-built for the hour — not just afterthoughts from the dinner menu. Order This:
  • Fried Lasagna — $12. That's the move. Nowhere else in Henderson is doing this.
  • Rigatoni alla Vodka — $12 happy hour portion. Made with Tito's, Calabrian chili on request.
  • Sicilian Old Fashioned — $10. Amaro Averna, Wild Turkey 101, spiced Demerara syrup. Serious cocktail for a happy hour price.
  • Any Spritz — $10 (Aperol, Cocchi Americano, or Italian Pink Lemonade with Ramazzotti Rosato).
Gaetano's opened in 2002 as one of the first fine dining restaurants in what was then a fast-growing part of Henderson, and the second generation — Nick and Sarah Palmeri — have earned Wine Spectator's Award of Excellence and certifications in mixology, spirits, and wine. The Reverse Happy Hour (8–9 PM daily) is the underrated move: 50% off full dinner entrées including the $60 filet and house made pastas, with any drink order. That's a $30 filet. Henderson locals already know. Now you do too. Bar happy hour daily 4–6 PM. Reverse happy hour daily 8–9 PM — bar seating, with a drink purchase. No coupons or offers stack with happy hour. Reservations recommended for dinner; bar is walk-in.

Boom Bang Happy Hour

Henderson (Green Valley) Happy Hour: Tue–Thu 4–6 PM | Fri–Sat 11:30 AM–6 PM

Here's what you need to know about Chef Elia Aboumrad before you order anything: she trained at Le Cordon Bleu, earned her Grand Diplôme, then went to Paris and became Joël Robuchon's first female Sous Chef. Then she moved to Las Vegas, ran kitchens at MGM Grand and Mandalay Bay, competed on Top Chef, won two Golden Knives on Food Network's 24 in 24: Last Chef Standing in 2025, and opened BoomBang in Henderson — where she is personally making house buns for the smash burger, juicing cocktail ingredients in-house, and having her pastry team hand-craft the garnishes. MenuPix

This is what a $8 smash burger looks like when a Robuchon-trained chef decides to make one.

The happy hour menu is the whole BoomBang philosophy at happy hour prices: Smash Burger (single $8, double $12) with grass-fed beef, house-made bun and their 999 sauce. Brocoli Cauliflower with Hot Rojo sauce and house ranch. Hummus with Salsa Macha, pickled onions, and pepitas. Thin Crust Pizza $12–$15. Cocktails $9, wine $7, draft beer $6. Everything made from scratch. Every cocktail ingredient juiced in-house. Clean, organic, artisanal — at bar prices.

Chef Elia describes BoomBang as "like Cheers — everyone knows each other, we know our guests well, and it feels like home yet away from home." Her motto: come and let us restore you. That's a restaurateur talking. You can feel the difference.

Order this: The double smash burger and a cocktail. Then the cauliflower. Then maybe the pizza. Friday and Saturday the happy hour runs from 11:30 AM to 6 PM, so you have time.

What's the story: A Top Chef veteran with Robuchon pedigree quietly running one of the best scratch kitchens in Henderson. The happy hour is how you get in the door without the dinner tab. Go.

post_content: The smartest seafood happy hour in Southwest Las Vegas might be sitting in a small strip mall with no casino attached. Other Mama Happy Hour has built a loyal following on oysters, creative raw bar plates, and cocktails that feel way more serious than the room’s laid-back vibe suggests. Industry people love this place for a reason. Order This: • Fresh Oysters — rotating selections, ice cold, and usually the first thing regulars order. • Lobster Mac — rich, cheesy, and somehow still balanced. • Blue Crab Hand Roll — simple, fresh, gone in three bites. • Any cocktail with Japanese whisky or mezcal. The bar program here quietly outperforms half the Strip. What is the happy hour at Other Mama? It’s a seafood-focused happy hour featuring oysters, sushi, small plates, and discounted cocktails in a casual neighborhood setting. That combination is harder to find in Vegas than you’d think. Most sushi happy hours lean cheap. Other Mama leans quality first, then keeps the prices approachable enough to come back often. The crowd tells you everything. Locals. Chefs on their night off. People who care about seafood but don’t need white tablecloths to enjoy it. The space stays lively without turning into a scene, and the menu changes just enough to keep regulars interested. Go early if you want bar seats—they disappear fast once happy hour starts rolling.
