post_content: A talking tiki head insults customers, there's vintage erotica in the bathrooms, and somehow this is still one of the most beloved bars in the city — Chinatown's Golden Tiki has been getting away with organized chaos for over a decade. The Golden Tiki's happy hour runs daily 4-7pm, and 1-4am with $6-9 tiki cocktails and $6 beer. Order This: the alcoholic Dole Whip for $8 — pineapple soft-serve spiked with real rum, not a syrup shortcut, and the drink regulars specifically wait for happy hour to order. Pair it with the Sticky Fingers, glazed fried chicken tenders that show up in review after review as the food people actually remember. Branden Powers, former creative director at Hard Rock Hotel, built this 4,000-square-foot fever dream with four themed lounges — the Pirates Lair, Mermaid Cove, Headhunter's Village, and a 20-foot waterfall behind the bar — and somehow the drinks are still legit rum-forward tiki cocktails, not sugar water in a coconut cup. That's the trick: Chinatown doesn't do the Strip markup, so a bar this theatrical can still pour a real mai tai for $8 during happy hour instead of the $18 version you'd pay a mile east. Reservations are for two-hour blocks and recommended on weekends — it gets loud and it gets full, and the tiki head does not care that you're waiting.

Le Thai Happy Hour One of the original restaurants that pulled people off Fremont Street Experience and into Fremont East — and it's still one of the best reasons to be there. Le Thai Downtown happy hour runs Mon–Thu 4–6pm and Saturday 11:30am–4pm with discounted appetizers, cheap Asian beer, wine, and cocktails at one of Downtown Las Vegas's most consistently praised Thai kitchens. Le Thai Happy Hour Menu with Prices
  • Waterfall Beef $12 — marinated strips of beef with sticky rice and the house waterfall sauce; the dish Time Out Las Vegas called "addictive" and the one happy hour regulars order first
  • Honey Garlic Wings $11 — Thai-style wings tossed in honey garlic sauce with sriracha ranch; the bar snack that earns its own fan base
  • Blooming Basil cocktail — gin, lime, and Thai basil; a reviewer called it "super refreshing" and ordered a second one immediately

Le Thai features an 800-square-foot beer garden and hosts local DJs, with a late-night menu running Thu–Sat. The happy hour is how you get in the door for less. This place fills up fast. 🌿 Happy Hour is Mon–Thu 4–6pm; Sat 11:30am–4pm. Located at 523 Fremont St. Street parking or paid lot nearby.

post_title: Wahoo's Fish Taco Happy Hour Centennial Hills
post_content: Pizza and sliders don't sound like fish taco territory, but that's exactly the move Wahoo's Tacos Centennial Hills adds to its happy hour lineup — a beach bar tavern that knows sports fans need more than tortillas. Order This: $2 street tacos are still the anchor here, same as every Wahoo's, but pair one with the sliders off the happy hour menu for something heartier. Add a $5 Wahoo's Margarita or a half off beer, and you've got a full spread for less than most Strip appetizers alone. Billed as a "Beach Bar Tavern & Gaming Cantina," this Tropical Parkway location leans hard into the sports-bar-meets-cantina identity — TVs on every wall, gaming machines at the bar, and a family-friendly split from the gaming area so kids aren't sitting next to slot machines. Centennial Hills isn't packed with sit-down chains that do both taco shop and sports bar well, so Wahoo's fills a real gap out here. Twice-daily happy hour means there's no excuse to skip it, whether you're catching the early game or closing out the night. Happy hour runs daily, 3-6 PM and 11 PM-2 AM. post_title: Rustic House Happy Hour Summerlin South
post_content:
If you're cruising around Summerlin South and craving a solid Happy Hour that goes beyond the basics, Rustic House might just become your new favorite spot. This laid-back, family-friendly neighborhood bar and restaurant knows how to keep the locals happy with great deals, generous portions, and a vibe that hits just right whether you're posted up at the bar, chilling in the lounge, or soaking in the fresh air on the patio. Daily Happy Hour That Actually Delivers Rustic House takes Happy Hour seriously—offering two every single day. The first runs from 4 PM to 6 PM, perfect for winding down after work or kicking off a fun night out. During this golden window, you can score: $7 starters (and we’re talking legit appetizers, not afterthoughts) $5 beers $6 well drinks $7 glasses of wine And if you're more of a night owl, you're in luck. Rustic House also serves a nightly Happy Hour from 9 PM to 7 AM, yes—50% off all drinks all night long. Whether you’re starting late or wrapping up a long shift, these prices are hard to beat in Summerlin. What to Eat? Go for the $7 Starters The Happy Hour menu might be short, but it packs a punch. These are fan favorites pulled right from their regular appetizer list (normally priced $11–$17), and now offered at just $7 during Happy Hour. Here are a few highlights:
  • Filet Nachos: A tower of tortilla chips loaded with pico de gallo, jalapeños, olives, guac, and their signature JC cheese sauce. Oh—and yes, it’s topped with filet mignon.
  • Dynamite Rolls: Spicy spring rolls stuffed with sesame chicken, cabbage, carrots, and sprouts. Served with a sweet chili dipping sauce that hits all the right notes.
  • Philly Fries: Imagine your favorite cheesesteak but on a bed of crispy fries. Shaved ribeye, mushrooms, onions, and more of that signature JC cheese sauce. It's pure comfort food.
These apps are perfect for sharing or not, depending on how hungry you are. Pair them with a cold draft or a glass of wine, and you’ve got yourself a budget-friendly mini feast.

The live music on Friday and Saturday nights (8PM–midnight) makes it a natural two-act evening: happy hour first, then stick around. If you want the full Johnny Mac's experience without the decades of wear-in at Boulder Hwy, this is the spot.

Stake Out Bar & Grill Happy Hour Las Vegas

If you're looking for a laid-back spot in Las Vegas to enjoy some drinks, munch on satisfying bar food, and hang out with good people, look no further than Stake Out Bar & Grill. This local favorite isn’t flashy or touristy—instead, it’s the kind of no-frills neighborhood bar where regulars know each other, the drinks are poured strong, and the Happy Hour hits just right. Located off the Strip, Stake Out has built a solid rep among locals for its chill atmosphere and great value. The place is cozy but lively, filled with pool tables, dartboards, and TVs playing everything from local sports to national games. It’s the kind of dive bar where you can stop in for a quick drink after work and end up staying a couple of hours without even realizing it. Now, let’s talk about Happy Hour—because that’s where Stake Out really shines.  Happy Hour runs twice daily 3pm-6pm and 12am-3am. The name might make you think of steaks—and yes, they do offer a hearty steak dinner—but the Happy Hour menu leans more into comfort food territory. Think crispy chicken wings, loaded nachos, cheeseburger sliders, and fried pickles. Everything is cooked to order, served hot, and generously portioned. It's bar food done right—greasy in the best way and super satisfying. Stake Out Bar & Grill, 4800 S. Maryland Pkwy 89119 Phone:  (702) 798-8383

If you're in the mood for a laid-back spot to grab a bite and a drink, Lucky's Tavern at PT's Taverns is your go-to destination. Located at Maryland Parkway & Cactus in Las Vegas, this neighborhood favorite offers a welcoming atmosphere, hearty food, and a great selection of drinks. Lucky's Tavern is known for its classic American fare with a twist. Whether you're craving a juicy burger, crispy wings, or a fresh salad, their menu has something for everyone. Whether you're a Las Vegas local or just passing through, Lucky's offers a comfortable setting to enjoy good food, drinks, and company. Ten-hour smoked brisket, biscuits with honey bourbon butter, and a happy hour that reviewers call the best in Vegas — on Water Street in Henderson. The Biscuits and Bourbon happy hour runs Sun–Thu 2–5pm and 2-4pm Sunday with drink specials and discounted bites at one of the most committed comfort food spots in the valley. Order This:
  • Biscuits with Honey Bourbon Butter & Hot Honey — the dish that defines the restaurant; reviewers say they transport you somewhere else entirely, and at happy hour they're the obvious first order
  • Bourbon Candied Pork Belly — center cut, caramelized, and the kind of thing that makes you reconsider your dinner plans
  • Smoked Wings — slow-smoked before they hit the fryer; a different animal from standard bar wings
  • Brisket Baked Beans — burnt ends folded into the beans; order these as a side or eat them alone, either works
  • Bourbon cocktails and draft beer at happy hour pricing (2–5pm Mon–Thu & 2-4 Sun)
Biscuits and Bourbon was opened by Henderson locals specifically to help revitalize Water Street, and it's working. The block has momentum now, and this place is part of why. The 10-hour smoked brisket, house-made biscuits, jam flights, and a bourbon list that backs up the name have built a loyal following that drives from across the valley. The happy hour price point makes it easy to come in, try four things, and understand immediately why people keep coming back. 🥃 Happy hour Mon–Thu 2–5pm and 2-4pm Sun. Open daily 8am–10pm. Located at 109 S Water St, Henderson. Outdoor seating available. *Note We have been unable to verify the happy hour menu. Call ahead before you make the trip.

$2 domestic beers and $3 wells — at the oldest bar in Henderson, open 24 hours on Water Street. The Gold Mine Tavern happy hour runs daily 2–6pm, making it one of the most generous happy hour structures in the valley at prices that feel like a different era. Order This:

post_content: You don’t need an Absinthe ticket to hang out at Green Fairy Garden inside Caesars Palace, and that’s the first thing locals should know. Hidden beside Spiegelworld’s circus chaos, this outdoor cocktail garden feels like old Vegas got weird in the best possible way—part absinthe lounge, part fever dream, part late-night hangout for people tired of casino bars. Technically, it’s not a happy hour. But the timing, pricing, and cocktail creativity absolutely earn it a spot on the list. Order This: the signature Green Fairy cocktail with absinthe, herbs, and citrus—strong, herbal, and not pretending to be subtle. The frozen espresso martini also gets a lot of repeat orders for good reason. Small plates rotate, but the fries and shareable snacks are the safest move if you’re drinking first and making decisions later. What is the happy hour at Green Fairy Garden? It’s more of an all-evening cocktail garden experience with approachable prices by Caesars Palace standards, creative drinks, and no show ticket required. That last part matters. Most people assume this area is only for Absinthe guests, which keeps the crowd smaller and the vibe looser than the casino floor outside. The whole setup feels intentionally offbeat—vintage carnival energy, live performers wandering through, cocktails arriving in theatrical glassware. Vegas needs more places like this. Grab a drink at sunset, stay longer than planned, and lean into the weirdness.

The Forum Shops location also means you're steps from Caesars' main floor, which makes this a natural stopping point before whatever comes next.

Zaytinya Happy Hour José Andrés' seventh Las Vegas restaurant opened at the Forum Shops in 2025 and runs Mediterranean happy hour twice daily, every day of the week. The Zaytinya happy hour at Caesars Palace, called Mezze Óra, features specially priced drinks and mezze bites in the bar and lounge during the first and last hour of service daily. Zaytinya Happy Hour Menu with Prices
  • Harissa Honey Wings ($15) — Mezze Óra pricing at a James Beard Award-winning chef's restaurant; order two
  • Garides Me Anitho: Sautéed Shrimp ($15) — Mediterranean-spiced, simply executed, and exactly the right small plate alongside a cocktail
  • Specialty cocktail ($12) — the Za'atar Margarita (Milagro tequila, orange liqueur, lime, za'atar air) is the one reviewers keep coming back to

Mezze Óra runs Mon–Thu 5–6pm and 8–9pm; Fri–Sat 11am–12pm and 9–10pm; Sun 5–6pm and 8–9pm — bar and lounge only. Zaytinya translates to "olive oil" in Turkish, and the concept — communal small plates drawing from Greek, Turkish, and Lebanese traditions — is one Andrés has been refining since 2002 in Washington, D.C. The Las Vegas location brings that same philosophy to the Forum Shops in an 8,600-square-foot room built for the kind of slow, shared meal that the Strip rarely delivers. Mezze Óra is the entry point. The $90 Chef's Experience tasting menu is where you go next. Bar and lounge only Mon–Thu 5–6pm and 8–9pm; Fri–Sat 11am–12pm and 9–10pm; Sun 5–6pm and 8–9pm . South Point locals have known about this spot for years. The combination of a real tequila program and a kitchen that takes its Mexican food seriously makes this one of the better south-end happy hour stops in the valley. 🌮 Thursday - Sunday Fiesta Happy Hour, Miguel's Tequila Bar only. post_title: Anthony's Prime Steak & Seafood Happy Hour
post_content:
A Wine Spectator Award winner in Henderson running a buy-one-get-one happy hour where you can mix and match — and the Las Vegas Advisor has called it one of the best deals in town. Anthony's Prime Steak & Seafood in Henderson doesn't get enough credit for this one.

The happy hour at Anthony's Prime Steak & Seafood runs daily 5–6PM, food only (no drink specials), with a buy-one-get-one deal across select menu items. Mix-and-match is allowed, so two people can order different things and one comes free.

Order This:

  • Clam Chowder — the standout according to every reviewer who's ordered it; Anthony's has always made an excellent version and it holds up
  • Oyster Rockefeller — cited repeatedly in reviews as a signature
  • Caesar Salad — a reliable anchor for the table during the BOGO window
  • Wedge Salad with blue cheese and thick smoked bacon — a diner favorite worth adding

The M Resort sits at 12300 S. Las Vegas Blvd., about 10 miles south of the Strip, which means the exhibition kitchen views include the Las Vegas skyline from a distance — a different perspective than you get anywhere else. The wine list runs 450 bottles deep with rare vintages back to 1961. The BOGO appetizer deal is the entry point; the housemade pasta is the reason you'll stay for dinner. 🍝 Located at M Resort, 12300 Las Vegas Blvd S, Henderson.

post_title: Lettys de Leticia Cocina Happy Hour
post_content:
Featured on Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives in 2023 and voted the most recommended Mexican spot in the Neon Feast survey by local chefs, restaurateurs, and food writers — Letty's de Leticia's Cocina in the Arts District has the kind of reputation that takes years to earn and no marketing budget to maintain. The Viva Happy Hour here is the most affordable way into one of downtown Las Vegas's best kitchens. The Letty's de Leticia's Cocina happy hour runs Monday–Thursday 3–6 PM and Fridays 3–5 PM, with 20% off appetizers, half off select cocktails, $5 imported beers, and $4 domestics. Order This:
  • La Fresca Margarita — the one featured on Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives. Half off during happy hour. Order it first.
  • Hibiscus Mezcal Cocktail — $half off. The most interesting drink on the happy hour list.
  • Nachotes — the happy hour version of the house specialty. Housemade corn tortilla chips, topped and finished the way only this kitchen does it.
  • Chicharrones — crunchy, salty, gone fast.
  • Ceviche — fresh, citrus-forward, exactly right for the Arts District patio energy.
Letty's occupies a building that once housed El Sombrero, one of Las Vegas's oldest Mexican restaurants — and the fact that Chef Leticia Mitchell chose that corner to open her downtown concept says everything about her commitment to the neighborhood. Her award-winning quesataco — seared cheese, chipotle crema, choice of protein — and the Quesabirria Pizza are the kind of dishes that people drive across the valley for. The happy hour is just the entry point. Once you're in, you'll stay for dinner. 🌮 Monday–Thursday 3–6 PM, Fridays 3–5 PM. Walk-ins welcome. Small room — go early.

Downtown Las Vegas runs late, and so does the happy hour at Nacho Daddy on N. 4th Street. Two windows — 3–6PM and again 9PM to close — which means this is one of the few places where happy hour pricing is still on the table at midnight.

The happy hour at Nacho Daddy Downtown runs Sunday through Thursday, 3–6PM and 9PM until close, with $5 drinks and discounted bites across the board.

Order This:

The Flamingo location is the brand's first Las Vegas outpost, and the happy hour is the accessible entry into a room that runs considerably more expensive at dinner. Reviewers specifically call out the mojitos from happy hour — go early, grab a seat at the bar, and order the croquettes. 🎶 Mon–Fri 4–6pm. Open daily 8am–midnight. post_content:
Fergusons Downtown Happy Hour Meets Community Vibes

Fergusons Downtown is more than just a cool corner of Las Vegas—it’s a whole community wrapped in good vibes, greenery, and great cocktails. Located in a renovated mid-century motel, Fergusons has transformed into a vibrant hangout where locals and visitors alike gather for art, live music, pop-up shops, and most importantly, some seriously solid Happy Hour action. If you're in the know, you’ve probably wandered into F The Bar, the cozy little cocktail spot right in the heart of Fergusons. The name alone sets the tone—irreverent, fun, and just a little cheeky. Their Happy Hour, offered daily from 6 to 8 PM, is a gift to cocktail lovers and budget-conscious sippers alike. Everything is $7 during Happy Hour—yes, everything. We’re talking beers, well drinks, margaritas, even some of their signature cocktails. There’s also a $4 mystery beer or seltzer listed as “Whatever the F,” which feels very on-brand and a little adventurous. Outside of Happy Hour, the cocktail list gets even more creative, with house specials like the Smokey Margarita made with 400 Conejos mezcal, and unique blends like the Rose Thorn, One Way Ticket, or Blossoms Up. These aren’t your average sugary bar concoctions—F The Bar leans into craft ingredients and thoughtful presentation without being pretentious. Whether you’re craving gin, mezcal, or something herbal and unexpected, the menu’s got you. The beer lovers aren’t left out either, with options like Hop Valley Bubble Stash IPA, Love Lady Mexican Lager, and Mojave Sunrise Blonde Ale on tap. Plus, there’s a solid lineup of canned beers and hard seltzers for $7. And when it comes to food, Fergusons is anything but predictable. Their sushi happy hour menu includes Mini Bites such as Coconut Shrimp ($8) and Crispy Rice ($7) giving visitors a sushi fix that’s light, social, and wonderfully in tune with the laid-back, community-minded vibe of the space. With string lights, picnic tables, live music, and a laid-back courtyard setting, Fergusons Downtown is the kind of place where Happy Hour turns into a whole evening. Whether you’re a cocktail enthusiast, food adventurer, or just looking for a good hang, Fergusons has the magic. For more Happy Hour deals, check our detailed guide to the best restaurants on The Strip, Off the Strip, Downtown Las Vegas, Henderson, and Summerlin that promise flavorful dishes and refreshing drinks.

Get there early if you want a good bar seat.

All American Sports Kitchen Happy Hour lands in the middle in a way that actually works: big screens, solid food, and a game-day energy that doesn’t feel forced. What is the happy hour at All American Sports Kitchen? Order This: • Gourmet Burger — juicy, stacked, and easily the standout of the menu. • Wood-Fired Pizza — crisp crust, melty cheese, built for sharing during a game. • Wings — classic game-day wings, saucy and dependable. • Loaded Nachos — tortilla chips, jalapeño, pico de gallo, crema and cheese.. It’s part of the Ahern Hotel setup, which keeps it slightly off the chaos of casino floors while still close enough to matter. It’s a solid pre-game, post-game, or “stay for three games” kind of stop. If you want Strip convenience without Strip nonsense, this is the move.

You're drinking cocktails made from spirits distilled on the same property — at a working craft distillery in Henderson that ships in water from out of state to get the flavor right. The Las Vegas Distillery happy hour runs Wednesday–Friday 3–5 PM, and it's one of the only happy hours in the valley where the booze in your glass was made fifty feet away. The Las Vegas Distillery happy hour features $2 off cocktails, spirit flights, pizza, and pretzels. The cocktail program is built around house-distilled spirits — vodka, rum, and coffee liqueur — all made on-site. Order This:
  • Espresso Martini — house coffee liqueur, Dark Moon espresso. The signature cocktail, and the most-cited drink by reviewers.
  • Barrel-Aged Old Fashioned — new make bourbon or white rum, aged in-house. The most interesting spirit-forward drink on the menu.
  • Spirit Flight — $2 off during happy hour. The right move if you've never tried the house spirits. Let the staff walk you through it.
  • Soft Pretzel Basket — from the bites menu, pairs well with anything on tap.
The distillery reopened in June 2024  after new owner Rob Saucier undertook a two-year top-to-bottom renovation. The happy hour is the low-commitment way to experience the tasting room without the full tour commitment. The atmosphere is described by reviewers as "quaint in the best way" — old Vegas style with modern craft sensibility. Henderson doesn't have many spots like this. Go on a Friday, order the espresso martini, and take the tour next time. 🥃

post_content: A 1962 dive bar that's open 24 hours and runs happy hour twice a day — once for the after-work crowd, once for the 2 a.m. shift change — is exactly the kind of place Strip tourists never stumble into. Nestled in the Arts District, this dive bar has been serving locals since 1962, and the Hard Hat Lounge happy hour is still where Downtown's industry workers go to unwind, whatever hour their shift ends. Order This: wells for $4, draft beer for $5, and PBR cans for just $3, poured into generous 22 oz mugs. Pair it with a smashburger from Stay Tuned Burgers, cited as some of Vegas' best by chefs James Trees, Nicole Brisson and David Varley — the kitchen inside the bar that turned a dive into a destination. This is what real Downtown happy hour culture looks like: construction workers get $1 off drinks all day, every day, and Strip workers get a 10% bar tab discount on Mondays during jazz night. No craft cocktail list, no DJ, no pretense — just a worn wood bar, neon, and a kitchen that out-burgers half the Strip. It's the kind of spot you mention once and someone says "wait, that's still open?" Yes. It's always open. Happy hour runs daily from 2 PM to 5 PM and again from 2 AM to 5 AM. No reservations, no cover — just walk in, day or night.

post_content:
Seed-oil free, anti-inflammatory, and $3 off all cocktails — at a nearly 11,000-square-foot restaurant inside the Forum Shops at Caesars Palace. The True Food Kitchen happy hour at Caesars Palace runs Mon–Fri 3–6pm with drink discounts and reduced prices on small plates, making it the healthiest happy hour option on the Las Vegas Strip. Order This:
  • Hummus $3 off  — house-made, fresh ingredients, the right start before anything else arrives
  • $3 Off Pizzas — brick oven, seasonal toppings, and the menu item that converts people who came in thinking this was just a salad restaurant
  • $3 Off Cocktails — the bar program at True Food runs clean spirits with fresh-pressed juices and no artificial mixers
  • $5 Beer or Proprietary Wine by the glass — the most straightforward happy hour order for the budget-conscious
Founded by integrative medicine pioneer Dr. Andrew Weil and 100% seed-oil free, True Food Kitchen is built entirely around the anti-inflammatory food pyramid — every ingredient selected for both flavor and function. The Forum Shops location is the brand's Strip flagship, a 11,000-square-foot room with an indoor patio, open kitchen, and two private dining rooms. The happy hour window is how you try the kitchen's seasonal cooking — quinoa bowls, brick oven pizzas, responsibly sourced proteins — without the full dinner tab. In a building full of indulgent Strip dining options, this is the option that makes you feel better walking out than walking in. 🌿 Located at The Forum Shops at Caesars Palace, 3500 Las Vegas Blvd S. This is a Kansas City Barbecue Society competition team running a neighborhood BBQ joint in Boulder City — and the meat goes on the smoker 10 hours before you arrive. Fox Smokehouse BBQ's happy hour runs Tuesday to Sunday 2–5 PM, which makes it one of the most frequent BBQ happy hours in the greater Las Vegas area. The Fox Smokehouse BBQ happy hour features $1 PBR, $5 select wines and cocktails, $0.99 wings, and $2 off all appetizers. The classic margarita has been spotted at $5 during happy hour and is worth ordering. Order This:
  • Brisket Sandwich — the most-reviewed item on the menu by a wide margin. Tender, properly smoked, on Texas toast. Order it as your anchor.
  • Wings at $0.99 — at that price, there's no reason not to add them.
  • $5 Classic Margarita — solid happy hour cocktail for a BBQ spot. Reviewers mention it by name.
  • Peach Cobbler — with vanilla ice cream and caramel drizzle. Not a happy hour item, but don't skip it.
Fox Smokehouse BBQ is a competition BBQ team — members of the Kansas City Barbecue Society, competing as "BBQ Junkie" on the circuit, with trophies and prize money to show for it. That background shows up on the plate: the rub is balanced, not overpowering, letting the quality of the meat carry the flavor. Boulder City is 30 minutes from the Strip and worth the drive specifically for this. When they sell out, they sell out — there's no second batch coming. Go before 5 PM and order the brisket first. 🍖 Happy hour runs Tuesday - Sunday 2–5 PM. Walk-ins only.

There are three smokers running at SNS Diner BBQ in North Las Vegas — one of them right in the middle of the open kitchen — and you smell it the moment you walk in. The SNS Diner BBQ happy hour runs Mon-Sat from 2–5pm with drink specials, and it pairs perfectly with some of the most from-scratch cooking in the valley. 🔥 Order This:
  • Smoked Meatballs — three brisket-gravy-smothered meatballs with Monterey Jack, served as a starter that earns its keep
  • Gravy Fries — fresh-cut, house-sliced fries buried under dark brisket gravy and melted Monterey Jack
  • Soup of the Day (Cup/Bowl) — Chef Mike rotates scratch-made soups like chicken sausage gumbo, pork posole, and New England clam chowder; whatever's on is worth ordering
  • Draft Beer — Shiner Bock, Kona Big Wave, Sierra Nevada Hazy, and more on tap at happy hour pricing (2–5pm)
SNS has been rated best BBQ in NLV, and it earns that by actually doing the work: red oak wood, slow-cooked meats, daily cornbread, and potato salad made in-house. This is a neighborhood restaurant that doesn't need the Strip to validate it. The people who know, know. If you haven't been, the happy hour window is a low-commitment way to find out why this place has a loyal following that drives from all over the valley. Happy hour drink specials run 2–5pm Mon-Sat.

Views of Red Rock, Snow, and Sheep mountain ranges from a golf course patio — with happy hour drink specials and bar bites in a smoke-free bar. The Durango Hills Golf Club Bar & Grill happy hour runs Mon-Thurs. Order This:

The Durango Grill patio faces the course and the surrounding mountain ranges, making it one of the more scenic places to have a midday drink in the northwest valley. You don't have to play golf to sit on the patio, though having a cold drink after 18 holes with that view is a very specific Las Vegas afternoon that's hard to replicate anywhere else. Confirm current drink specials directly before visiting — the daily rotation changes. 🏌️ Happy Hour available 3- 6pm. Located at 3501 N Durango Dr, Las Vegas. Public course — no membership required.

The creator of the Penicillin cocktail is a consulting partner — and his fingerprints are on a craft cocktail bar that opened in Downtown Las Vegas in late 2025 with a hidden speakeasy in the back. The White Whale happy hour at Fremont East runs Mon–Fri 4–6pm with discounted craft cocktails made with daily-squeezed juices and house-made syrups. Order This:
  • White Whale Dirty Martini — fat-washed Botanist Gin or Haku Vodka, kombu, MSG; the signature cocktail that earns the reviews it gets
  • Spicy Sammy — Don Julio Blanco, Aperol, lime, Firewater Tincture; the cocktail that casual and serious drinkers both reach for
  • Black Friday — Wild Turkey 81, vanilla extract, egg whites, lemon; the spirit-forward option for anyone who wants something richer
  • Captain's Quarters experience — no menu, no set drinks; tell the bartender your mood and they build something custom. Find the door with the whale stencils on the brick.
White Whale occupies the former Downtown Cocktail Room space at 111 S Las Vegas Blvd — an address that defined Las Vegas's craft cocktail scene for years. Partners Daniel Yang and Evan Hosaka, veterans of Wakuda and the Cocktail Collective, built this room around Sam Ross's philosophy: the bar takes the craft seriously but never itself. The happy hour is how you walk in without planning and walk out a regular. The Captain's Quarters speakeasy in the back is what brings you back the second time. 🐋 Mon–Fri 4–6pm; Located at 111 S Las Vegas Blvd, corner of Las Vegas Blvd and Fremont East.

All-you-can-eat tacos for $20 — daily, 3–6pm, on Fremont Street, from the same team behind Evel Pie across the street. The Taco Escobar happy hour runs every day from 3–6pm with $4 draft beer, $5 wells, $6 house margaritas, and two tacos plus a beer for $8 — and the AYCE deal makes it one of the most straightforward value propositions in Downtown Las Vegas.

Order This:

  • $20 AYCE Street Tacos — one-hour time limit, four tacos at a time, cilantro and onion
  • 2 Tacos + 1 Beer ($8) — the lighter entry point if you’re bar-hopping and not ready for a full AYCE session
  • $6 House Margarita — cold, simple, and the right call before or during the AYCE window

Taco Escobar is from Lev Group, the hospitality company also behind Evel Pie across the street, and the Lucha Libre luchador mascot theme runs through everything from the branding to the menu names. Six proteins are available for the tacos, and the scratch-made approach — slow-cooked birria, chicken tinga, marinated steak, and famous mushrooms — backs up the happy hour pricing with actual quality. Fremont East is the right neighborhood for this kind of place: relaxed, local-leaning. The $20 AYCE deal is the reason to show up at 3pm rather than later.

Happy hour daily 3–6pm. Located at 509 Fremont St, Downtown Las Vegas. (702) 600-0378.

The Griffin Happy Hour

The Griffin on Fremont Street in Downtown Las Vegas offers a cozy, old-school bar experience with a touch of vintage charm. Featuring a classic jukebox, two glowing firepits, and dim, moody lighting, this local favorite is the perfect spot to unwind with a drink, enjoy good music, and soak in the nostalgic atmosphere of a true downtown gem.

The Griffin Happy Hour Location & Hours

The Griffin is located on 511 Fremont St, at Las Vegas Blvd. S. No website but check their Instagram page or give them a call 702-382-0577. Happy Hours at the Griffin 6 PM to 7 PM and 1 AM to 2 AM.

The Griffin Happy Hour Menu with Prices

  • Craft Beer
  • Stiff Drinks

What is the Vibe at the Griffin Happy Hour?

The vibe at The Griffin during Happy Hour is cool, moody and effortlessly relaxed. With its vaulted brick ceilings, deep-red leather booths, and two glowing firepits, the atmosphere leans more cozy crawl-bar than flashy club. Guests often describe it as a “locals’ hideaway” on Fremont Street—free of the big-tourist energy of the Strip, yet still decidedly downtown Vegas in style. Music is low enough to allow conversation, with indie and rock tracks from a vintage jukebox setting the tone rather than pumping bass. In short: if you want a happy hour stop that’s relaxed but full of character—firepits, good drinks, and a comfortable crowd—The Griffin hits that mark.

Conclusion

The Griffin’s Happy Hour offers a laid-back yet atmospheric escape in the heart of Fremont Street. With its vintage jukebox, warm firepits, and inviting old-school charm, it’s the perfect place to enjoy a drink, unwind with friends, and experience a more relaxed side of downtown Las Vegas nightlife.

A $12 Petite Filet Mignon sandwich and $5.50 beers — at a convention-corridor steakhouse that's been feeding Las Vegas business dinners for decades. The Morton's Steakhouse Power Hour runs Sun–Fri 4–6:30pm in the Bar area, with  $9 wine by the glass, $10 craft cocktails, and a dedicated bar bites menu that delivers steakhouse quality at bar prices. Order This:
  • Petite Filet Mignon Sandwich $12 — the Power Hour signature; hand-cut filet on a toasted roll; the steakhouse happy hour item that earns every review it gets
  • Smash Burger Sliders $12 — the casual alternative; well-executed, properly priced, and the right call if you want something more substantial
  • $10 Craft Cocktail — the bar program at Morton's leans classic; order a proper Old Fashioned and let it anchor the Power Hour
  • $5.50 Beer / $9 Wine — the most straightforward pricing on the menu; Bud Light, Heineken, Miller Lite, and a non-alcoholic option from Athletic Brewing
The restaurant sits near the Las Vegas Convention Center on Paradise Road, which means the bar fills early with a mix of convention business and locals who know the deal. Dress code is enforced — proper attire required — but the bar area is where you want to be anyway. No reservation needed for Power Hour; walk in and grab a seat before 6:30pm. 🥩 Located at 400 E Flamingo Rd.  (702) 893-0703.

$3 street tacos and a Hot Cheetos-infused tequila margarita for $8 — through a secret tunnel in the back of a taco shop in Chinatown. The Mas Por Favor happy hour runs daily 3–6pm with $3–$7 bites and cocktails, $15 sangria pitchers, and $20 margarita pitchers at one of the more distinctive setups on Spring Mountain Road. Order This:
  • Signature Tacos ($4 each) — reviewers call these the best on the menu; tender, well-seasoned pork with pineapple; order three
  • Hot Cheetos Infused Tequila Margarita ($8 HH) — one reviewer called it "very different" and ordered a second one; the signature drink that nobody else in Vegas is making
  • Guava Margarita ($8 HH) — refreshing, fruity, and the safer call if the Hot Cheetos version sounds like too much commitment
  • $20 Margarita Pitcher — the group order; get one on arrival and let everyone pour their own
  • Pho-Kin Taco ($4 HH) — the fusion signature; Vietnamese-Mexican crossover that only works in a city like this one
Mas Por Favor opened in January 2020 in Chinatown — which says everything about where Las Vegas's creative dining energy was heading even before the pandemic. You order at the front counter, eat tacos, and then ask the cashier about "tonight's delight" to access the speakeasy through a hidden tunnel in the back wall. It's a legitimate concept that earns its own press coverage, including a featured mention in USA Today for its National Tequila Day promotions and a Las Vegas Review-Journal piece on its holiday speakeasy events. Spring Mountain Road at 3pm, secret door in the back, $4 tacos. You're welcome. 🌮 Located at 3879 Spring Mountain Rd, Chinatown. Walk-ins welcome; reservations available for the speakeasy.

All-you-can-eat prime rib for $49.99 at a proper Strip steakhouse. That's not a typo, and it's not a loss-leader gimmick — it's the headliner deal at Jack Binion's Steak inside Horseshoe Las Vegas, and it's the reason this place deserves more attention than it gets.

Order This:

  • All-You-Can-Eat Prime Rib — $49.99 — slow-roasted, carved tableside on return rounds; reviewers note later rounds can be sliced thinner, so go early and go often.
  • $7.77 Jackpot Features — classic Vegas pricing on a rotating set of bites and drinks including a Steak Slider, Shrimp Cocktail, Wedge Salad, Hot Fudge Sundae, and a Vodka Martini — all $7.77 each
  • The Boss's Old Fashioned — the bar is worth a stop before you sit down; Las Vegas Magazine called it a recommended order.

The happy hour at Jack Binion's Steak isn't a traditional happy hour — it's a set of all-day value features that punch well above their price point for a mid-Strip steakhouse. The room channels old-school Vegas with muted tones, vintage photographs from early Las Vegas, and waitstaff who make you feel like a regular — even on your first visit. The happy hour at Nine Fine Irishmen isn't a happy hour — it's better. The newly renovated patio at this Strip-side Irish pub inside New York-New York now runs $7 bar bites and $5 drink specials all day, every day, with a front-row seat to Las Vegas Boulevard and the shadow of a replica Brooklyn Bridge overhead.

Order This:

  • Mini Shepherd’s Pie - Ground Beef, Peas, Carrots, Onions, Mashed Potatoes
  • $5 pints — Guinness, Harp, Smithwick's — poured correctly, which matters more than you'd think on the Strip

What makes this worth knowing: Nine Fine Irishmen was literally built in Ireland and shipped over, and the pub feels like it. A recent renovation by DEZMOTIF Studios expanded the patio out onto Brooklyn Bridge Plaza, and the result is one of the few outdoor drinking spots on the Strip that actually has personality. No cover, no time limit, no "happy hour window" to stress about. The all-day format is rare here — most Strip properties use time-based deals to control foot traffic. This one just... doesn't. Come for a pint at noon or at sunset. Either works.

The $7 bar bites and $5 drink specials are available on the outdoor patio only. The pub itself is open Sunday–Thursday 11am–1am and Friday–Saturday until 2am. No reservations needed for the patio.

Echo Taste Happy Hour offers a modern and inviting atmosphere where guests can unwind with creative cocktails and flavorful bites. "Where Flavor, Vinyl & Community Collide in Downtown Vegas"

Echo Happy Hour Location & Hours

Echo is located at 1301 S Main St. in the Arts District, Las Vegas. Echo Happy Hours run Wednesday through Friday 5 PM to 7 PM. Visit Echo or phone 702-268-7466

What is the Dress Code for Echo Taste Happy Hour?

What is the Vibe at Echo Happy Hour?

Here’s the vibe you can expect at ECHO Taste & Sound — a lounge-happy-hour destination in Las Vegas that blends music, craft cocktails and a comfortable yet elevated feel:

  • Sophisticated but relaxed — The space is described as “wood-paneled, ’70s-style rec room of a deep-pocketed audiophile” thanks to the vintage and high-end stereo gear that powers the music.

  • Music as the focus — This isn’t just background noise. The sound system is hi-fi, with vinyl records, curated playlists (jazz, soul, funk) and intention behind the music selection.

  • Elevated small plates & cocktails — While you can relax and sip, there’s also a menu of refined food and drink created to pair with the listening experience.

  • Arts District energy — Located in the downtown Las Vegas Arts District, the setting conveys creative, urban and slightly off-the-main-strip feel; ideal for something different than the usual nightclub rush.

  • Approachable, not intimidating — Though the sound system and design are high-end, the atmosphere is described as approachable. “We’re not trying to alienate; we’re really trying to introduce and embrace".

Do I need to make a reservation for Echo Happy Hour?

For the Echo Taste & Sound happy hour, reservations are not strictly required, but they are available and recommended, especially if you’re visiting with a group or want a guaranteed seat.

The venue holds some seating open for walk-ins, so if you arrive early, you may be able to get a table without a reservation.

For larger parties (8 or more), they ask that you email their reservations team. For more information please visit their website or phone 702-268-7466.

Final thoughts

Echo Taste Happy Hour offers a refined yet laid-back experience that blends exceptional sound, inventive cocktails, and flavorful small plates. Whether you’re winding down after work or meeting friends for an evening out, it’s a stylish destination that celebrates both taste and music. With its relaxed smart-casual dress code, welcoming vibe, and convenient reservations, Echo Taste & Sound stands out as one of Las Vegas’ most unique and enjoyable happy hour spots.

The only authentic Maryland-style crab house on the West Coast — and it's been quietly feeding East Coast transplants and Las Vegas seafood lovers since 2010. The Crab Corner happy hour, called "Don't Be Crabby Hour," runs daily 2–6pm and is headlined by one of the best single-item deals in town. Order This:

Two brothers from Maryland noticed Las Vegas had no real crab house and fixed that problem in 2010. Weekly specials go deep: all-you-can-eat blue crabs on Mondays, $2 crabs and beers on Tuesdays, whole Maine lobster with two sides on Wednesdays, and $3 crabs and beers on Thursdays. The patio, the full bar, and the pile of blue crabs on butcher paper make this feel nothing like Las Vegas — which is exactly the point. If you've never picked a blue crab in your life, the staff will show you how. 🦀 Daily 2–6pm, seven days a week. Located at 6485 S Rainbow Blvd, Ste 104. Open 11am–9pm daily.

D'Agostino's Happy Hour

A 12-inch Neapolitan pizza for $10, a house made draft brewed just for them, and a happy hour that skips Monday entirely because they'd rather be closed than mediocre. D'Agostino's Trattoria, tucked into the corner of Buffalo and Flamingo off the Strip, is quietly running the best happy hour pizza on the west side.

D'Agostino's Happy Hour Menu with Prices

The Classic Neapolitan Margherita ($10) — pomodoro, fresh mozzarella, hand-torn basil, blistered in a proper pizza oven — is the anchor, but don't stop there. Pair it with the Pancetta Wrapped Dates ($10) or the "Sterner the Burner" Shrimp Scampi ($10), colossal shrimp in a Cajun-spiced white wine butter sauce that earns its name. Drinks run $10 for cocktails, $10 by the glass for wine, and $6 for D'Agostino's own house draft.

This is what an off-Strip Italian happy hour looks like when the kitchen actually cares: real charcuterie boards, scampi-style clams, a wine list that isn't an afterthought. It's not chasing tourists — it's built for locals who want a proper trattoria bite without a Strip markup, and the Board & Bottle at $35 practically dares you to make a night of it. Southwest Vegas doesn't get enough credit for its food scene, and this is exactly why it should.

Happy hour runs Tuesday through Sunday, 4-6pm — closed Mondays. No reservation required, but the bar fills up fast on weekends.

Drinking a frozen daiquiri under a thatched roof inside a medieval castle sounds made up, but that's exactly what MGM built when it dropped its first-ever tiki bar into Excalibur. The happy hour runs every single day, which puts it ahead of most Strip bars that only bother on weekdays. The Tiki Bar's happy hour runs daily from 5-7pm with $8 tiki specialty cocktails and frozen daiquiris, plus $5 domestic beers and $6 imports. Order This:
  • Whip Tai — pineapple whip on top, built for the photo before the sip
  • Buzzed Tiki Torch — RumChata, Fireball, coffee liqueur, and banana liqueur, which sounds chaotic and mostly works
  • A Tiki Flight if you can't commit to just one
Excalibur spent three decades as the Strip's budget castle, so a tropical bar next to the MGM Rewards desk shouldn't work on paper — dragon lore and lava rock walls next to a jousting arena is a genuinely weird pairing. But that's the trade-off: full-price tiki drinks here run $17-18, so the daily two-hour window is the only reason to actually order one. It's not trying to out-craft The Golden Tiki, and it doesn't need to — it's a cheap, campy sit-down option for anyone staying at Excalibur, Luxor, or Mandalay Bay who doesn't want to leave the property. No cover, no reservation needed — just walk in off the casino floor. Live music kicks in around 9pm on weekends, but the happy hour pricing itself runs every day of the week, castle theme included.

post_content: A steakhouse happy hour in Southwest Las Vegas usually means one of two things: tiny portions or watered-down drinks. Butcher & Thief Happy Hour avoids both. Frozen margaritas made with Espolon tequila, poured at a walk-up bar right off the Treasure Island casino floor. No host stand, no table, no fuss. 🍹

Dress is casual and the average check runs about $20 a person. Find it on the Strip side of the casino, next to Starbucks. Grab a frozen one and go from there.

post_title: F1 Arcade (50% Off Nevada Residents Only)
post_content:
F1 Arcade Las Vegas 50% Off For Nevada Residents

NEVADA RESIDENTS ONLY - Beginning April 1 and continuing through Aug. 30, 2026, Nevada locals can enjoy 50% off a wide selection of its tempting food and beverages, creating an even more compelling opportunity for Las Vegans to experience one of the Strip’s most dynamic entertainment venues. This is not an official happy hour however, it feels like a happy hour in every way and only available to Nevada residents. Designed to be an irresistible invitation for the local community to discover F1 Arcade, the offer includes half off drinks, including draft beer, well liquor with mixers, seltzers, house red and white wine by the glass as well as signature cocktail pitchers filled with spirited libations concocted by Netflix “Drink Masters” champion LP O’Brien.

F1 Arcade Happy Hour Menu with Prices

Guests can also enjoy 50% off a range of menu favorites, including sharing plates, tacos, flatbreads, burgers, salads and desserts. F1 Arcade’s culinary program takes inspiration from cities around the world and includes items such as Korean Gochujang Cauliflower Wings; Himalayan Salt Dry-Aged Flat Iron Steak with grilled portobello and chimichurri; Quesabirria with three chili consommé, Oaxacan cheese and cilantro; Chipotle Tiger Shrimp with pickled daikon, cucumber, ginger and ponzu; Caprese Flatbread with basil pesto, cherry tomatoes and fresh burrata; Spicy Ahi Tuna Tacos with avocado, wasabi, scallions, sesame, cilantro and red chili; and a Hazelnut and Chocolate Calzone with toffee sauce and vanilla ice cream. Known for combining elevated hospitality with high-energy entertainment, F1® Arcade allows guests to step into the driver’s seat on 87 full-motion racing simulators, competing against friends on world-famous Formula 1® circuits while enjoying globally inspired cuisine and craft cocktails. Large-format screens, vibrant lighting and a lively social atmosphere create a venue designed for groups, celebrations and spontaneous nights out alike. The Nevada resident promotion is available Monday through Thursday from 5 p.m. to close and Friday through Sunday from 1 p.m. to close, giving locals plenty of opportunities to experience the venue whether after work, during weekend outings or while hosting visiting friends. To redeem the offer, guests must present a valid Nevada driver’s license or ID to their server or bartender upon arrival. Each Nevada ID may be used for up to four guests at the table. The promotion excludes select menu items including the 40-oz. Angus Tomahawk and raw bar offerings, including the Seafood Tower. F1 Arcade Las Vegas is open 12 p.m. to 12 a.m. Monday through Thursday, 12 p.m. to 1 a.m. Friday, 10 a.m. to 1 a.m. Saturday and 10 a.m. to 12 a.m. Sunday. The venue invites guests of all ages until 9 p.m. daily and is open for guests 21 and older after 9 p.m. It is located at 3500 South Las Vegas Boulevard inside The Forum Shops at Caesars Palace. Follow @f1arcadeusa on Instagram for the latest updates and special events.

The Krazy Samurai and Philadelphia rolls consistently show up as reader favorites if you're going the à la carte route instead. Centennial doesn't get the sushi density of the Strip or Chinatown, so a spot doing fresh fish daily, a full bar, and a real happy hour window this far northwest is doing real work for the neighborhood. This is a restaurant locals default to specifically because it's close, it's not trying to be fancy, and it's been consistent for over 15 years — the kind of reliability that's rarer than the "best sushi in Vegas" claims floating around Yelp reviews would suggest. Reservations aren't typically required — walk in, grab a bar seat if you're there for happy hour, and check the posted menu for the day's specials since pricing can shift.

post_title: Michoacán Gourmet Mexican Restaurant Happy Hour
post_content:
Northwest Vegas has had a reliable margarita stop on Tropical Parkway since 2009, and the happy hour price is $8. It's a sit-down Mexican restaurant with a bar that has a real tequila list, not a strip-mall pour. The happy hour at Michoacán Gourmet Mexican Restaurant in Centennial Hills runs 2 to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday. House margaritas are $8 ($11 for a jumbo), house wine and well drinks are $7, and beer is $4.50 for imports and domestics or $5.50 for draft. Order This:
  • Cadillac Margarita, $10 ($14 jumbo): the upgraded pour, and worth the extra $2.
  • Nachos, $9.50: the easy shareable for the table.
  • Sopitos, steak or chorizo, $10.
  • Popcorn Shrimp, $7 for 6 pieces or $10 for 12.
  • Gorditos Camarones, $11.50: the priciest bite on the menu, and a full plate.
This is a neighborhood happy hour built for locals, not tourists. It's close to home for the northwest valley, the parking is easy, and it costs about half what a Strip margarita does. The restaurant has offered "hundreds" of tequilas for years, so if the house pour gets boring, there's room to explore. One caveat: happy hour is weekdays only, so don't plan a Saturday around it. Show up at 2, order the Cadillac, and settle in with the nachos.

post_content: Two hours of golf, food, and drinks for $49, and no tab to check afterward. ⛳ The happy hour at Atomic Golf in Las Vegas, at 1850 S. Main St near the Strat, is an all-inclusive package, not a drink discount. It runs Monday through Friday, with two-hour start times between noon and 4 p.m. Each person pays $49. On Friday and Saturday from 9 p.m. - 12 a.m., you can enjoy the Late Night Unlimited package for $59 per person. Order This: The Happy Hour Unlimited package. It includes a reserved golf bay, unlimited play, unlimited draft and canned beer, wine, and cocktails, and unlimited food from the happy hour menu. Think tacos, sliders, and shareable small plates. You can add an extra hour for $25 per person. The math is the point. If you'd order a couple of rounds and a plate of food anyway, the flat price covers it, and you get a bay of interactive golf on top. It's built for groups, which is why a work crew or birthday table can go all-in without splitting a check. The caveat is that this is a package deal, not a per-drink discount, so it pays off for people who eat and drink. Food comes one entrée per person at a time, and party platters aren't included. For a late-night version, the Reverse Happy Hour runs Friday and Saturday from 9 p.m. to midnight for $59. Book a bay, pick your crew, and plan your two hours.

Glitter Gulch Tiki Happy Hour feels like stepping into a neon fever dream designed by someone who actually respects old-school tiki culture—but isn’t afraid to turn the volume up. Bamboo, carved wood, thatched booths, and a dance floor that looks ready for trouble. What is the happy hour at Glitter Gulch Tiki? It’s a Downtown Las Vegas tiki bar happy hour with discounted tropical cocktails, punchy rum drinks, and playful island-style bites in an immersive neon-lit lounge. Order This: 🍹 Mai Tai Monday features the Mai Hands Tai’d, the venue’s take on a classic Mai Tai made with rhum agricole, dark rum, orange curaçao, lime and orgeat, priced at $7 throughout the day. 🍹 Tiki Tuesday specials from 4 to 7 p.m., featuring $7 signature cocktails,. $7 Dole soft serve cocktails, $7 beers and $7 wine. Dole soft serve cocktails include the Na’cho Whip, made with Rum Haven Coconut, orange juice, coconut, passion fruit and guava; Lili of the Valley, made with Telsón Blanco tequila, coconut, lime and passion fruit; and Dr. Meyers Revenge, featuring Dole soft serve spun with dark and spiced rums. Signature cocktails include Tiki Passion Obsession, made with Bacardi Black rum, Chinola passion fruit liqueur, Giffard orgeat, hibiscus and lime and The Old Jamaican, made with Appleton Estate Signature VX rum, Clément Mahina Coco liqueur, spiced demerara, bitters and a flaming lime. 🍹 Wednesday through Friday happy hour $12 classic cocktails, $10 frozen cocktails and $5 beers and wine. Classic cocktails include standouts such as David’s Revenge, made with Telsón Añejo tequila, crème de cassis, lime, prickly pear and ginger beer; Luau in Vegas, featuring Telsón Reposado tequila, banana liqueur, falernum, coconut cream, pineapple and lime with a float of overproof rum; and Makula Retrograde, made with Tanqueray Seville Orange gin, passion fruit, orgeat, lychee and lemon. This place exists because Downtown Vegas still has room for personality. Not everything has to be casino lounge minimalism or Strip luxury polish. Glitter Gulch leans all the way into themed excess, but with actual design intent—Bamboo Ben details, performance space energy, and a vibe that feels like Fremont Street grew a tiki obsession overnight. The crowd is a mix of locals, cocktail nerds, and people who came for one drink and stayed for three. That’s the danger here. Come early if you want a seat that isn’t standing room by the bar.

post_content: Good beer in Boca Park isn’t hard to find. Good beer brewed by people who actually studied the craft? That narrows the list fast. Nevada Brew Works Happy Hour delivers the kind of happy hour locals appreciate—fresh beer, straightforward pricing, and food that goes beyond the usual pub filler. What is the happy hour at Nevada Brew Works? It’s a Boca Park brewpub happy hour featuring discounted house-brewed beers, cocktails, and appetizers in a laid-back taproom setting built for hanging out. Order This: • Beer Flight — the smartest first move. Sample the house lineup and find your favorite. • Atomic Duck IPA — one of the local standouts and a regular crowd favorite. • Cheese Curds — crisp, salty, and built for beer. • Jalapeno Peppers— simple, tasty, and exactly right with a pint. It’s the kind of place where happy hour can turn into dinner without much debate. Start with a flight, settle on a pint, and stay awhile. The beer earns it. post_content:
If you're craving a solid Happy Hour that goes beyond the basics, Rustic House at Silverado Ranch might just become your new favorite spot. This laid-back, family-friendly neighborhood bar and restaurant knows how to keep the locals happy with great deals, generous portions, and a vibe that hits just right, whether you're posted up at the bar, chilling in the lounge, or soaking in the fresh air on the patio. Daily Happy Hour That Actually Delivers Rustic House takes Happy Hour seriously—offering two every single day. The first runs from 4 PM to 6 PM, perfect for winding down after work or kicking off a fun night out. During this golden window, you can score: $7 starters (and we’re talking legit appetizers, not afterthoughts) $5 beers $6 well drinks $7 glasses of wine And if you're more of a night owl, you're in luck. Rustic House also serves a nightly Happy Hour from 9 PM to 7 AM, yes—50% off all drinks all night long. Whether you’re starting late or wrapping up a long shift, these prices are hard to beat in Summerlin. What to Eat? Go for the $7 Starters The Happy Hour menu might be short, but it packs a punch. These are fan favorites pulled right from their regular appetizer list (normally priced $11–$17), and now offered at just $7 during Happy Hour. Here are a few highlights:
  • Filet Nachos: A tower of tortilla chips loaded with pico de gallo, jalapeños, olives, guac, and their signature JC cheese sauce. Oh—and yes, it’s topped with filet mignon.
  • Dynamite Rolls: Spicy spring rolls stuffed with sesame chicken, cabbage, carrots, and sprouts. Served with a sweet chili dipping sauce that hits all the right notes.
  • Philly Fries: Imagine your favorite cheesesteak but on a bed of crispy fries. Shaved ribeye, mushrooms, onions, and more of that signature JC cheese sauce. It's pure comfort food.
These apps are perfect for sharing or not, depending on how hungry you are. Pair them with a cold draft or a glass of wine, and you’ve got yourself a budget-friendly mini feast.

post_content: Guy Fieri's Vegas Kitchen & Bar Happy Hour Flavortown doesn't stop at 8pm, it just gets a happy hour discount. Guy Fieri's Vegas Kitchen & Bar at The LINQ runs its happy hour nightly starting at 8pm, and it leans into Guy's actual UNLV roots instead of just slapping his name on generic bar food. Guy Fieri's Vegas Kitchen & Bar Happy Hour Menu The Sidewinder fries are crispy, tossed in spicy buffalo seasoning, topped with blue cheese crumbles, served with house buffalo sauce and a blue cheese-wasabi "blu-sabi" dip. Also on the menu: a pulled pork slider stacked with Guy's bourbon brown sugar BBQ sauce, citrus slaw, pickle chips, aged cheddar, and onion straws on a pretzel bun — billed as a throwback to Guy's UNLV days, plus achiote chicken or carne asada tacos with guac and salsa roja. This isn't a quiet neighborhood happy hour,  it's Strip-front, patio-facing, and built for people who want people-watching with their wings. The UNLV nod matters here: Guy Fieri went to school in Las Vegas before he became a national brand, and this menu is one of the few places on the Strip that actually plays that up instead of treating him like a licensing deal. It's a reminder that even the biggest celebrity-chef spots on Las Vegas Boulevard can still have a real local thread running through them, if you know where to look. Happy hour runs daily from 8pm until close, with seating both indoors and on the 6,500-square-foot Strip-view patio. No reservation required, though the full dinner menu differs from the happy hour version — some guests have been disappointed a specific dish (like fish and chips) wasn't available during the discounted hours, so check before you set your heart on something specific.

post_content: Off the Strip near the convention center, this cantina runs one of the most generous taco specials in the city — $3 street tacos, six days a week, no gimmicks attached. Marufuku Ramen took over the old SkinnyFATS space at Downtown Summerlin, and unlike most Japanese happy hours in town that vanish after Friday, this one holds steady daily from 2-5pm. Cocktails run $8 (Old Fashioned, Iced Lychee Martini, Matcha Martini), wine is $5 (Cabernet, Brut, Sauvignon Blanc), and Sapporo or Asahi drafts are $5 a pour.
